literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.

The available observational evidence did not show a clear increase in mortality among transferred compared with non-transferred COVID-19 ICU patients. None of the adjusted effect estimates showed a statistically significant mortality disadvantage for transferred patients. [10.1038/s41598-026-62965-7]

The vaccine effectiveness was 75% (95% CI 70%–79%) overall, with higher effectiveness in individuals previously vaccinated in 2023–2024 (84%, 95% CI 80%–87%) compared to those without prior vaccination (65%, 95% CI 34%–82%). [10.1038/s41467-026-76312-x]

Among naturally infected individuals, the IgG-positivity rate was higher for N (80.9%) than S (42.8%), with significantly elevated N-specific IgG levels compared to prepandemic controls (p-value <0.05). [10.1177/08828245261474281]

Engineered variants of CC65.1 showed newly acquired MERS-CoV-neutralizing activity, with high-resolution structural studies revealing that key mutations reshape the paratope to better accommodate and stabilize the MERS-CoV S2 stem helix, resulting in increased binding affinity and neutralization potency. [10.1371/journal.ppat.1014393]

news.lead_zh: 本期SARS-CoV-2新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 世卫组织文件概述了严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2及其变异株的全球风险评估,并讨论在刚果民主共和国(DRC)遏制埃博拉暴发的紧急行动需求。该事件为一项风险评估及行动呼吁,由世界卫生组织报告。 [news-a815b938afc0cfcb]

A study published by the American Hospital Association (AHA) found that COVID-19 can reactivate dormant viruses. This is a reported finding based on a study, not an outbreak or confirmed event. [news-4fe25e145c22a643]
The article discusses the origin and characteristics of SARS-CoV-2, the virus that causes COVID-19, including its transmission, symptoms, and impact on global health. [news-4ea3b0adeb4441ee]
《自然》杂志的一项研究报告称,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染可以在免疫功能正常的个体中重新激活休眠的慢性病毒(指环病毒科、疱疹病毒科),持续的指环病毒活性与 长新冠 身体缺陷有关;研究结果挑战了重新激活主要发生在免疫抑制患者中的观点(N3、N4、N44)。 [news-b20a607f2121aaf7]
RF.5 Omicron 变种与浦​​那的 Covid 感染有关,废水 监测 表明自 2026 年 7 月第一周以来病毒载量有所增加。这是由州卫生部门报告并得到国家病毒学研究所证实的。 [news-acd9aaab54f447fd]

key_findings_en: The WHO document outlines a global risk assessment for SARS-CoV-2, including its variants, and discusses the need for urgent action to contain the Ebola outbreak in the DRC. The event is a risk assessment and call for action, reported by the World Health Organization. [news-a815b938afc0cfcb]

A Nature study reports SARS-CoV-2 infection can reactivate dormant chronic viruses (Anelloviridae, Herpesviridae) in immunocompetent individuals, with persistent Anelloviridae activity linked to long COVID physical deficits; findings challenge the view that reactivation occurs mainly in immunosuppressed patients (N3, N4, N44). papers.title: Risk Factors of the Spread of COVID-19 in Prisoners: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to identify and synthesize evidence on risk factors for COVID-19 in incarcerated populations. METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar was conducted for English articles until October 2025. Study quality was assessed using the PRISMA checklist and NOS tool. Meta-analysis was performed in Stata 17 using a random-effects model, with odds ratios as the primary effect measure and statistical significance set at P < 0.05. Heterogeneity was evaluated via I2 statistics. RESULTS: Twelve articles were ultimately included in the study. For the meta-analysis, only 5 articles were considered, which evaluated sex, age, and vaccination status as the risk factors of COVID-19. The total sample size was 176169, consisting of 169117 males and 7,726 females. In most studies, the average age was reported to be around 40 years. Fully vaccinated prisoners were less likely to contract COVID-19 than unvaccinated ones (OR: 0.38; 95% CI: 0.22, 0.67; P = 0.001), while no significant relationships were found regarding sex and age. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings confirm that full vaccination significantly protects against COVID-19 in prisons. Prioritizing vaccination campaigns, along with measures like mask use and hand hygiene, is essential to protect incarcerated individuals and the wider community.
papers.journal: Disaster Medicine and Public Health Preparedness

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigated risk factors for the spread of COVID-19 in incarcerated populations. A comprehensive search of PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar was conducted up to October 2025, and study quality was assessed using the PRISMA checklist and NOS tool. Twelve articles were included, with a total sample size of 176,169 individuals, predominantly male. The meta-analysis focused on five studies evaluating sex, age, and vaccination status as risk factors. papers.title: Convalescent Plasma Restores Viral Clearance After Anti-Spike Monoclonal Antibody Failure in Immunocompromised COVID-19 Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Individual Patient Data.
papers.abstract: Anti-Spike monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) progressively lost efficacy during the COVID-19 pandemic due to the emergence and predominance of resistant SARS-CoV-2 variants. By contrast, high-titre COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) collected from vaccinated donors recently recovered from infection provides a polyclonal source of antibodies that remains effective in clearing SARS-CoV-2 in immunosuppressed patients, unable to mount an adequate immune response against the virus. We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis to examine the effect of CCP in immunocompromised patients persistently positive for SARS-CoV-2 viraemia following mAb therapy, and to evaluate possible biological factors associated with a favourable outcome. Electronic databases were searched for studies published from January 2020 to January 2026. All studies including eligible cases were considered in the systematic review. Unpublished cases were also collected from investigators of the selected studies. The protocol was registered at PROSPERO (CRD420251142891). Forty-seven cases (30 cases from 12 published studies and 17 unpublished cases) were included. In 33 out of 47 patients (70.2%) with a mAb-resistant infection, SARS-CoV-2 clearance occurred following CCP transfusion, with a mean of 2.7 CCP units administered. In logistic regression, total CCP volume transfused was positively associated with SARS-CoV-2 clearance. In conclusion, CCP transfusion was associated with SARS-CoV-2 clearance in persistently positive immunocompromised patients following failure of anti-Spike mAb therapy.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated convalescent plasma (CCP) as a rescue therapy for immunocompromised COVID-19 patients with persistent SARS-CoV-2 viraemia after anti-Spike monoclonal antibody (mAb) failure. Across 47 cases, CCP achieved viral clearance in 70.2% of patients, with higher transfusion volumes associated with improved outcomes. The review highlights CCP as a potential polyclonal alternative to mAbs in resistant infections, though small sample size, unpublished case inclusion, and variant-specific data gaps limit generalizability. Key priorities include randomized trials to confirm efficacy, variant-stratified analyses, and enhanced surveillance to track CCP performance against evolving SARS-CoV-2 variants.

papers.title: Timing, Titre, and Host Determinants of Convalescent Plasma Efficacy in COVID-19: A Systematic Review With Design-Stratified Narrative Synthesis.
papers.abstract: The efficacy of convalescent plasma (CP) in COVID-19 has been contested, with large randomized trials producing conflicting results that led to recommendations against routine use. We performed a systematic review with design-stratified narrative synthesis (PRISMA 2020; SWiM; OSF: https://osf.io/tjcuq) to test whether these conflicting outcomes can be reconciled through three interacting determinants-timing, antibody titre, and host characteristics-using a standardized 91-field extraction matrix applied to each study. PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched through May 2026. Thirty-one studies (20,793 patients; 8 RCTs, 23 observational) were included. The synthesis indicates that CP is effective, but only under a specific convergence of conditions: when administered early in the disease course, with sufficient antibody titre, to seronegative or immunocompromised hosts who have not yet mounted an endogenous antibody response. Among RCTs analysing timing, 4 of 6 found benefit with earlier administration; for titre, 3 of 4 RCTs with explicit comparisons found benefit with higher-titre CP; and two large RCTs (combined n = 12,522) demonstrated preferential benefit in seronegative recipients. This interpretation is consistent with modelling estimates that CP, deployed largely to hospitalised patients, nonetheless saved tens of thousands of lives in the United States during the first pandemic year, an effect attributed to the subset treated early enough to modify disease progression. A second, previously unquantified finding concerns antibody class: characterisation of non-IgG immunoglobulins was nearly absent, with only 2 of 31 studies-both from our group-reporting IgA or IgM data, despite evidence that IgA and IgM are among the most potent neutralising classes against SARS-CoV-2. This hypothesis-generating observation identifies a systematic gap in CP product assessment. These findings reframe CP efficacy from a binary question to a conditional one and provide a template for the precision deployment of passive immunotherapy in future pandemics.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review investigates the efficacy of convalescent plasma (CP) in treating COVID-19, focusing on three key determinants: timing of administration, antibody titre, and host characteristics. The review includes 31 studies (20,793 patients; 8 RCTs, 23 observational) and employs a design-stratified narrative synthesis approach. The analysis suggests that CP is effective under specific conditions, such as early administration, high antibody titre, and use in seronegative or immunocompromised individuals. However, the review highlights a significant gap in the characterization of non-IgG immunoglobulins, as only two studies reported IgA or IgM data. The findings emphasize the need for targeted use of CP and suggest a framework for its precision deployment in future pandemics.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: The efficacy of convalescent plasma (CP) in COVID-19 has been contested, with large randomized trials producing conflicting results that led to recommendations against routine use.
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 我们通过设计分层叙述综合(PRISMA 2020;SWiM;OSF:https://osf.io/tjcuq)进行了系统评价,以测试是否可以通过三个相互作用的决定因素(时间、抗体滴度和 宿主 特征)来调和这些相互冲突的结果,并使用应用于每项研究的标准化 91 场提取矩阵。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 合成结果表明,CP 是有效的,但仅在特定条件下有效:在病程早期,以足够的抗体滴度,对尚未产生内源性抗体反应的血清阴性或免疫功能低下的 宿主 进行给药。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 第二个先前未量化的发现涉及抗体类别:几乎不存在非 IgG 免疫球蛋白的表征,尽管有证据表明 IgA 和 IgM 是针对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的最有效中和类别之一,但我们小组的 31 项研究中只有 2 项研究报告了 IgA 或 IgM 数据。这一假设生成观察发现了 CP 产品评估中的系统性差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 这些发现将CP疗效从二元问题重新定义为条件问题,并为未来大流行中精确部署被动免疫疗法提供了模板。

papers.title: Inter-hospital ICU-to-ICU transfer of critically ill COVID-19 patients is not associated with increased mortality: a systematic review with exploratory meta-analysis
papers.abstract: During the COVID-19 pandemic, inter-hospital transfer of critically ill patients between intensive care units was widely used to manage capacity shortages. While several individual studies have compared outcomes of transferred and non-transferred patients, no systematic synthesis of this evidence exists. This systematic review aims to determine whether inter-hospital ICU-to-ICU transfer of adult COVID-19 patients is associated with increased mortality or other adverse clinical outcomes. We systematically searched PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus for observational studies comparing clinical outcomes of adult COVID-19 patients who underwent inter-hospital ICU-to-ICU transfer with non-transferred ICU patients. Two reviewers screened, selected, and extracted data independently and in duplicate. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and ROBINS-I, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. Exploratory random-effects meta-analyses were performed separately for each effect measure, with Hartung-Knapp and crude-effect sensitivity analyses. Nine observational studies from seven countries were included (approximately 6,100 transferred and 29,200 non-transferred ICU patients). None of the adjusted effect estimates showed a statistically significant mortality disadvantage for transferred patients. Pooled adjusted subgroup estimates were an odds ratio of 1.29 (95% CI 0.84 to 1.98; k = 3) and a hazard ratio of 0.71 (95% CI 0.34 to 1.46; k = 2). Length of stay was longer in transferred patients in most studies. The available observational evidence did not show a clear increase in mortality among transferred compared with non-transferred COVID-19 ICU patients. These findings support the use of inter-hospital transfer as a safe strategy for managing ICU surge capacity. PROSPERO CRD420261356915.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review investigates whether inter-hospital ICU-to-ICU transfer of critically ill adult COVID-19 patients is associated with increased mortality or adverse clinical outcomes. The review included nine observational studies from seven countries, covering approximately 6,100 transferred and 29,200 non-transferred ICU patients. The findings indicate that the available observational evidence did not show a clear increase in mortality among transferred patients. None of the adjusted effect estimates demonstrated a statistically significant mortality disadvantage. Pooled subgroup estimates showed an odds ratio of 1.29 (95% CI 0.84 to 1.98) and a hazard ratio of 0.71 (95% CI 0.34 to 1.46), suggesting no consistent evidence of increased mortality. However, the review notes that length of stay was longer in transferred patients in most studies, and there are unresolved issues regarding study design, patient severity, and hospital resources. The results support the use of inter-hospital transfer as a safe strategy for managing ICU surge capacity during the pandemic.

papers.source_body_en: During the COVID-19 pandemic, inter-hospital transfer of critically ill patients between intensive care units was widely used to manage capacity shortages. papers.title: Allosteric effects of CDR-H3 mutations modulate binding and neutralization of a conserved SARS-CoV-2 RBD-targeting antibody
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: SARS-CoV-2 antigenic evolution continues to erode the activity of first-generation monoclonal antibodies, underscoring the value of antibodies that recognize conserved features within the spike receptor-binding domain (RBD). As a model for breadth-oriented engineering, we assessed the RBD-directed antibody XG83, which has a CDRH3-dominated paratope. Utilizing the XG83-Wuhan RBD crystal structure as a reference, we integrated MOE alanine scanning and residue scanning with CDRH3 (A116-Y132) to identify chemically reasonable replacements and test interaction to an Omicron BA.1 RBD. The parental CDRH3-centric pose in comparative docking had a better score (-280.18) than the mutant MuXG83 (-254.2), along with 100-ns molecular dynamics showed that MuXG83 was less stable (with higher RMSD/RMSF with less favorable interaction energy). The ELISA results against Omicron BA.1 RBD demonstrated that XG83 had 40% stronger binding than MuXG83; convergence happened only at the highest concentration, concordant with SPR studies and the fact that mutation increased dissociation. According to this binding gap, BA.1 pseudovirus neutralization demonstrated that XG83 was much more powerful than MuXG83, showing that the E118L/F130H CDR-H3 alterations decreased functional activity against Omicron BA.1. These results imply that allosteric influences on interface stability and conformational dynamics by non-epitope CDR-H3 residues can affect antibody performance. Functional testing was confined to Omicron BA.1; therefore, larger variant-panel studies are needed to ascertain if such mutations affect antibody breadth. Our findings highlight a structure-guided approach for optimizing paratopes and indicate that non-epitope (potentially allosteric) changes to CDRH3 are also important while investigating potential development and neutralization before advancement. IMPORTANCE: This study shows how modest allosteric characteristics in CDR-H3 control the delicate balance between neutralizing potency and breadth, making a timely and significant addition to SARS-CoV-2 antibody engineering. Using crystallography, alanine scanning, residue scanning, docking, molecular dynamics, and experimental ELISA and neutralization assays, this study offers a structure-guided framework for rational paratope optimization. The discovery of CDR-H3 residues that regulate long-range stability rather than just direct epitope contacts reveals an unappreciated aspect of antibody design and explains why some alterations improve anticipated interactions but degrade functional performance. Importantly, the comparison of wild-type XG83 and modified MuXG83 shows how allosteric tuning affects antibody-antigen compatibility in developing variations like Omicron. These findings illuminate conserved RBD recognition and offer strategies for building next-generation therapeutic antibodies that are more resistant to viral evolution.

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,非表位 CDRH3 残基对界面稳定性和构象动力学发挥变构作用,从而调节抗体性能。他们强调,这种变构调整是抗体设计中一个未被充分认识的方面,揭示了尽管改善了预测的相互作用,但细微的变化如何会意外地降低功能活性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现证明 CDRH3 的变构调节可以增强对病毒 进化 的抵抗力,为下一代治疗抗体的工程设计提供了信息。这种方法可以指导针对新兴 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体具有更广泛中和能力的抗体的开发。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于针对 Omicron BA.1 的功能测试,因此对其他变体的影响广度存在不确定性。证据是温和的,因为结论是基于单个变体,并依赖于通过实验分析验证的计算预测,需要在更广泛的变体小组中进一步验证。

papers.title: Critical role of vaccination in preventing severe coronavirus disease 2019: perspectives from clinical outcomes in an Australian kidney transplant recipient cohort
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Kidney transplant recipients (KTRs) disproportionately experience severe COVID-19 infections. We previously identified concern regarding vaccine-induced rejection as a barrier to vaccine uptake. AIM: This study assesses COVID-19 vaccine uptake, infection outcomes and allograft rejection in KTRs during the delta and omicron waves (BA.1/BA.2). METHODS: This cohort study included all adult KTRs with a functioning allograft at 22 March 2021 at our centre. KTR and vaccination-related risk factors for the primary outcome of severe COVID-19 infection (requiring hospitalisation) and the secondary outcomes of death and all COVID-19 infections were assessed using Cox proportional hazards models. Rejection risk following infection/vaccination was also assessed. RESULTS: Of the 986 included KTRs, there were 333 (33.8%) COVID-19 infections, 79 (23.7%) severe infections and 13 deaths (n = 13/333, 3.9%). Vaccine number was the most significant modifiable predictor of severe infection (adjusted hazards ratio, per additional dose, 0.5; 95% confidence interval, 0.40-0.65, P < 0.001) and death. While older age also predicted severe infection and death, lower estimated glomerular filtration rate, history of diabetes and previous allograft rejection predicted severe infection. Male gender was the only predictor of all infections. Mycophenolate dose, prednisolone use and vaccine type did not predict infection or severe disease. Infections and vaccinations did not increase the risk of rejection. CONCLUSIONS: KTRs should be encouraged to be optimally vaccinated to prevent severe disease and can be reassured about the low risk of allograft rejection. Risk factors that compound the state of immunocompromise and severe COVID-19 infections should prompt vigilance and targeted interventions to mitigate these risks.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Kidney transplant recipients (KTRs) face disproportionately severe outcomes from COVID-19, and vaccine hesitancy due to concerns about allograft rejection may further increase risk. This study aimed to quantify COVID-19 vaccine uptake, infection outcomes, and rejection risk in KTRs during the Delta and Omicron waves.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cohort study was conducted at a single centre, enrolling all adult KTRs with a functioning allograft as of 22 March 2021. The study period covered the Delta and Omicron (BA.1/BA.2) waves.
analysis.methods: Vaccination status and KTR-related risk factors were assessed using Cox proportional hazards models to determine predictors of severe COVID-19 infection (hospitalisation), death, and all infections. Rejection risk following infection or vaccination was also evaluated.
analysis.main_results: Among 986 KTRs, 333 (33.8%) had COVID-19 infections, 79 (23.7%) were severe, and 13 deaths occurred (3.9%). Each additional vaccine dose reduced the risk of severe infection (adjusted hazards ratio 0.5; 95% CI 0.40–0.65; P < 0.001) and death. Older age, lower eGFR, diabetes, and prior allograft rejection predicted severe infection, while male gender predicted all infections. Vaccine type and immunosuppressant doses did not predict outcomes, and neither infections nor vaccinations increased rejection risk.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrates that higher vaccine uptake significantly reduces severe COVID-19 and mortality in KTRs without increasing rejection risk, addressing concerns about vaccine-induced allograft damage. This provides direct clinical evidence supporting optimal vaccination in this high-risk group.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support prioritising vaccination in KTRs to prevent severe disease and mortality, while reassuring clinicians and patients about the low risk of rejection. Targeted interventions for immunocompromised patients with compounding risk factors are warranted.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The single-centre design and lack of randomisation limit generalisability and causal inference. However, robust statistical adjustment and clear outcome definitions strengthen the evidence. The study provides moderate-strength evidence for vaccine efficacy in KTRs.

analysis.summary_en: This cohort study of 986 kidney transplant recipients (KTRs) assessed COVID-19 outcomes during the Delta and Omicron waves, focusing on vaccine uptake, severe infection, mortality, and allograft rejection. Vaccination was the strongest modifiable predictor of reduced severe disease and death, with each additional dose halving the risk (adjusted HR 0.5; 95% CI 0.40–0.65; P < 0.001). Older age, diabetes, lower kidney function, and prior rejection also increased severe infection risk, while male gender predicted any infection. Vaccine type and immunosuppressant doses did not influence outcomes, and neither infections nor vaccinations increased rejection risk. The study concludes that KTRs should be optimally vaccinated to prevent severe COVID-19 and can be reassured about rejection risk. Limitations include a single-centre design and observational nature, but robust statistical methods support the findings.

papers.title: Intravenous immunoglobulin recalibrates monocyte responses to abortive SARS-CoV-2 infection across viral variants
papers.abstract: Monocytes contribute to inflammation during coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), yet their capacity to support productive infection by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), and the impact of viral evolution on their responses, remain unclear. Here, we investigated the interaction between primary human monocytes and three SARS-CoV-2 variants representing distinct evolutionary stages (Wuhan, Delta, and Omicron), and evaluated the modulatory effects of intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg). All variants efficiently entered monocytes and persisted as intracellular viral RNA and protein, but failed to generate infectious progeny, indicating abortive infection. Despite the absence of productive replication, infected monocytes exhibited marked ultrastructural remodeling and mounted robust innate immune responses. Omicron infection was associated with enhanced replication-related signatures compared with Wuhan and Delta. IVIg did not prevent viral entry or RNA persistence but significantly reduced infection-induced vacuolization and selectively modulated cytokine responses. Notably, high-dose IVIg enhanced TNF-associated responses and reduced IL10 expression, suggesting a recalibration of monocyte inflammatory set-points. These effects occurred independently of neutralizing activity. Together, these findings identify primary human monocytes as targets of abortive yet immunologically active SARS-CoV-2 infection and demonstrate that IVIg modulate monocyte stress and inflammatory responses through Fc-dependent mechanisms rather than direct viral neutralization.

The research highlights that all variants efficiently enter monocytes but fail to produce infectious progeny, indicating abortive infection. papers.title: Comparative immunogenicity of mRNA-1273 and BNT162b2 SARS-CoV-2 bivalent booster vaccines in US nursing home residents.
papers.abstract: Nursing home residents (NHRs) remain among the most vulnerable to severe outcomes from SARS-CoV-2 infection. While mRNA-1273 (Spikevax, Moderna) and BNT162b2 (Comirnaty, Pfizer-BioNTech) vaccines are widely used in this population, comparative data on their immunogenicity, particularly after bivalent boosters, remain limited. We conducted a longitudinal immunologic evaluation of U.S. NHRs who received either the mRNA-1273 or BNT162b2 bivalent vaccine. Serum samples were collected 10-30 d post-vaccination. Anti-spike IgG levels were measured using a Luminex bead-based assay, and neutralizing titers were assessed via pseudovirus neutralization. Comparative analyses of the titer distributions were performed using two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum tests. Both vaccine groups demonstrated strong humoral responses to the ancestral Wuhan strain and Omicron BA.4/5 subvariants. Spike-binding antibody levels and neutralization titers were comparable between the mRNA -1273 and BNT162b2 vaccine formulations. Conclusions: Both mRNA-1273 and BNT162b2 mRNA vaccines elicit similarly robust humoral immunity in NHRs, supporting their interchangeable use in booster strategies. Our findings underscore the importance of timely booster administration over exact product selection in protecting this high-risk, immunosenescent population.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated humoral immunogenicity of mRNA-1273 and BNT162b2 bivalent booster vaccines in U.S. nursing home residents, a population at high risk for severe SARS-CoV-2 outcomes. papers.title_zh: mRNA-1273 和 BNT162b2 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 二价加强剂 疫苗 在美国疗养院居民中的免疫原性比较。
papers.source_body_en: Nursing home residents (NHRs) remain among the most vulnerable to severe outcomes from SARS-CoV-2 infection. While mRNA-1273 (Spikevax, Moderna) and BNT162b2 (Comirnaty, Pfizer-BioNTech) vaccines are widely used in this population, comparative data on their immunogenicity, particularly after bivalent boosters, remain limited. We conducted a longitudinal immunologic evaluation of U.S. NHRs who received either the mRNA-1273 or BNT162b2 bivalent vaccine. Serum samples were collected 10-30 d post-vaccination. Anti-spike IgG levels were measured using a Luminex bead-based assay, and neutralizing titers were assessed via pseudovirus neutralization. Comparative analyses of the titer distributions were performed using two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum tests. Both vaccine groups demonstrated strong humoral responses to the ancestral Wuhan strain and Omicron BA.4/5 subvariants. Spike-binding antibody levels and neutralization titers were comparable between the mRNA -1273 and BNT162b2 vaccine formulations. Conclusions: Both mRNA-1273 and BNT162b2 mRNA vaccines elicit similarly robust humoral immunity in NHRs, supporting their interchangeable use in booster strategies. Our findings underscore the importance of timely booster administration over exact product selection in protecting this high-risk, immunosenescent population.

papers.title: Reviewer #2 (Public review): Nanoscopy reveals heparan sulfate clusters as docking sites for SARS-CoV-2 attachment and entry
papers.abstract: Abstract Virus entry is thought to involve binding a unique receptor for cell attachment and cytosolic entry. For SARS-CoV-2 underlying the COVID-19 pandemic, angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) is widely considered the receptor for cell-surface attachment and cytosolic entry. Using advanced light microscopy to resolve individual virions and receptors, we found instead that heparan sulfate (HS), not ACE2, mediates SARS-CoV-2 cell-surface attachment and subsequent endocytosis. ACE2 functions only downstream of HS to enable viral genome expression. Instead of binding single HS molecules that electrostatically interact with viral surface proteins weakly, SARS-CoV-2 binds clusters of ∼6–137 HS molecules projecting 60–410 nm above the plasma membrane. These tall, HS-rich clusters, present at about one per 6 μm2, act as docking sites for viral attachment. Blocking HS binding with the clinically used HS-binding agent pixantrone strongly inhibited an authentic pathogen, the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron JN.1 subvariant, from attaching to and infecting human airway cells. This work establishes a revised entry paradigm in which HS clusters mediate SARS-CoV-2 attachment and endocytosis, with ACE2 acting downstream, thereby identifying HS interactions as a key anti-COVID-19 strategy. This paradigm and its therapeutic implications may apply broadly beyond COVID-19 because, analogous to SARS-CoV-2, HS binds many other viruses but is only considered an attachment regulator. Statement of Significance Viral entry, a crucial antiviral target, is typically thought to involve binding its unique receptor for the cell surface attachment and subsequent entry. We examined this concept with advanced microscopies to resolve individual receptors and SARS-CoV-2 virions responsible for the COVID-19 pandemic. We discovered two receptors for viral entry: heparan sulfate, a polysaccharide that may bind many viruses, mediates viral attachment and subsequent endocytosis, whereas angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2), the generally assumed SARS-CoV-2 receptor, acts only downstream to facilitate viral infection. This model suggests perturbation of HS binding as a more effective anti-COVID-19 strategy than previously recognized. It may apply broadly beyond COVID-19 because, analogous to SARS-CoV-2, HS binds many other viruses but is only considered an attachment regulator.

Using advanced light microscopy to resolve individual virions and receptors, we found instead that heparan sulfate (HS), not ACE2, mediates SARS-CoV-2 cell-surface attachment and subsequent endocytosis. ACE2 functions only downstream of HS to enable viral genome expression. Instead of binding single HS molecules that electrostatically interact with viral surface proteins weakly, SARS-CoV-2 binds clusters of ∼6–137 HS molecules projecting 60–410 nm above the plasma membrane. These tall, HS-rich clusters, present at about one per 6 μm2, act as docking sites for viral attachment. Blocking HS binding with the clinically used HS-binding agent pixantrone strongly inhibited an authentic pathogen, the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron JN.1 subvariant, from attaching to and infecting human airway cells. This work establishes a revised entry paradigm in which HS clusters mediate SARS-CoV-2 attachment and endocytosis, with ACE2 acting downstream, thereby identifying HS interactions as a key anti-COVID-19 strategy. This paradigm and its therapeutic implications may apply broadly beyond COVID-19 because, analogous to SARS-CoV-2, HS binds many other viruses but is only considered an attachment regulator. Statement of Significance Viral entry, a crucial antiviral target, is typically thought to involve binding its unique receptor for the cell surface attachment and subsequent entry. We examined this concept with advanced microscopies to resolve individual receptors and SARS-CoV-2 virions responsible for the COVID-19 pandemic. We discovered two receptors for viral entry: heparan sulfate, a polysaccharide that may bind many viruses, mediates viral attachment and subsequent endocytosis, whereas angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2), the generally assumed SARS-CoV-2 receptor, acts only downstream to facilitate viral infection. This model suggests perturbation of HS binding as a more effective anti-COVID-19 strategy than previously recognized. It may apply broadly beyond COVID-19 because, analogous to SARS-CoV-2, HS binds many other viruses but is only considered an attachment regulator.

papers.title: Plasma concentrations of nirmatrelvir and molnupiravir required for inhibition of SARS-CoV-2 replication differ between rhesus macaques and humans
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Early during the COVID-19 pandemic, non-human primate (NHP) infection models emerged as highly useful tools for preclinical screening of antiviral drugs. However, it is uncertain whether NHP models can be used to precisely inform optimal dosing in humans. We previously established and validated mathematical models, which were fit to SARS-CoV-2 viral loads from human clinical trials. These models identified that plasma drug concentrations required to inhibit viral replication by 50% in humans ( in vivo EC50) differ substantially from in vitro EC50 estimates in cell culture systems. Here, we apply models to sequential viral load data from SARS-CoV-2 infected rhesus macaques (RMs) that were untreated or treated with nirmatrelvir/ritonavir, molnupiravir, or both drugs. We identify that equivalent plasma drug concentrations correspond to greater antiviral potency in the lungs compared with nasal passages for nirmatrelvir and molnupiravir. Average nirmatrelvir antiviral efficacy in RM (30% in nasal passages and 46% in the lungs) was estimated to be less than in humans (82%) due to shorter plasma drug half-life. Molnupiravir efficacy in RMs (95% in nasal and 99% in the lungs) is estimated to be similar to efficacy in humans against omicron variants. Our model estimates that 10-fold higher plasma nirmatelvir concentrations are needed in humans versus RMs to achieve 50% reduction in viral replication, whereas 20-fold lower plasma molnupiravir concentrations are needed. Our results suggest that dose optimization in humans based on modeling of NHP viral loads is limited by drug-specific differences in pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, and virologic profiles, and that data from human phase 1 and 2 trials are better suited for this task.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed whether non-human primate (NHP) infection models can precisely inform optimal dosing of antiviral drugs in humans during the COVID-19 pandemic. It highlighted uncertainty in translating NHP-derived antiviral efficacy to human dosing requirements for SARS-CoV-2.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study applied mathematical models to sequential viral load data from SARS-CoV-2 infected rhesus macaques (RMs) that were either untreated or treated with nirmatrelvir/ritonavir, molnupiravir, or both drugs. The models were previously established and validated using SARS-CoV-2 viral loads from human clinical trials.
analysis.methods: Mathematical models were fit to SARS-CoV-2 viral loads from human clinical trials to estimate plasma drug concentrations required to inhibit viral replication by 50% in humans. These models were then applied to viral load data from SARS-CoV-2 infected rhesus macaques to estimate antiviral efficacy and required drug concentrations.
analysis.main_results: Equivalent plasma drug concentrations corresponded to greater antiviral potency in the lungs compared with nasal passages for both nirmatrelvir and molnupiravir. Average nirmatrelvir antiviral efficacy in RMs was estimated at 30% in nasal passages and 46% in the lungs, lower than the 82% efficacy estimated in humans due to a shorter plasma drug half-life.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that dose optimization in humans based on NHP viral load modeling is limited by drug-specific differences in pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, and virologic profiles. They concluded that human phase 1 and 2 trial data are better suited for determining optimal dosing.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings caution against directly extrapolating NHP-derived antiviral efficacy to human dosing, emphasizing the need for human trial data to inform drug dosing strategies for SARS-CoV-2. This has implications for the design of preclinical studies and the translation of antiviral efficacy from animal models to clinical practice.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study acknowledges that dose optimization in humans based on NHP modeling is constrained by drug-specific differences in pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, and virologic profiles. The evidence strength is moderate due to reliance on modeling and the limited generalizability of NHP data to humans.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated whether non-human primate (NHP) models can accurately inform optimal dosing of antiviral drugs for SARS-CoV-2 in humans. Using mathematical models previously validated with human clinical trial data, the authors analyzed viral load data from SARS-CoV-2 infected rhesus macaques treated with nirmatrelvir/ritonavir, molnupiravir, or both. They found that antiviral efficacy and required drug concentrations differed between NHP and humans, with nirmatrelvir showing lower efficacy in RMs (30–46%) than in humans (82%) due to shorter drug half-life. Molnupiravir efficacy was similar between RMs and humans. The authors concluded that NHP-derived antiviral efficacy cannot be directly translated to human dosing and that human phase 1–2 trial data are essential for dose optimization.

papers.title: The impact of expanded adolescent vaccination against COVID-19 depends on the epidemic status: a mathematical modelling study
papers.abstract: Abstract Background/ObjectivesWe evaluated the impact of the COVID-19 adolescent vaccination in England at two different epidemic points: the autumn (August-November) 2021, in the presence of a large Omicron epidemic wave, and the autumn (August-November) 2022, when the subsequent Omicron epidemic was at an endemic stage. MethodsUsing the Covasim SARS-CoV-2 model for England, under varying vaccine uptake and onset time, we evaluated the impact of a)vaccinating 18+ only versus additional 12+ vaccination from the autumn 2021; and b)the current immunisation strategy at the time versus additional 12+ vaccination from September 2022, projecting the number of new daily SARS-CoV-2 infections, hospitalisations and deaths. ResultsIn presence of the BA.1 Omicron wave in late 2021, the expanded adolescent vaccination averted 3,000,000 cases across all-ages, 1,010,000 SARS-CoV-2 infections in the period 2-6 months from vaccine onset in the vaccinated cohort. During the Omicron waves in 2022, additional adolescents vaccination did not significantly reduce the COVID-19 burden in the entire population, nor within the vaccinated cohort. ConclusionsOur findings highlight that adolescent vaccination impact depends on the timing/speed of implementation, other present intervention strategies, and the status of the epidemic at the time and it should not be considered as a stand-alone immunisation strategy. HighlightsO_LIFirst study to compare the impact of expanding adolescent COVID-19 vaccination at two different epidemic points: one when a large epidemic is spreading and another at a more endemic stage of the epidemic. C_LIO_LIIn autumn 2021, in the presence of the newly emerging Omicron variant, adolescent vaccination was necessary to curb infections in both the adolescent cohort and the overall population. C_LIO_LIEarlier implementation at sufficient coverage was more effective in reducing the number of infections at the peak of the Omicron wave, and getting ahead of the epidemic spread. C_LIO_LIIn autumn 2022, when the Omicron epidemic was at an endemic stage, adolescent vaccination was not necessary to curb infections in both the adolescent cohort and the overall population. C_LIO_LIOur work shows that implementation, timing and speed of an adolescent immunisation programmes should be considered in conjunction with the epidemic status, incidence and prevalence of the epidemic at that time.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate how the impact of adolescent vaccination against SARS-CoV-2 varies depending on the epidemic status, specifically during the Omicron wave in late 2021 and its endemic phase in 2022.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A mathematical modelling study using the Covasim SARS-CoV-2 model for England assessed the impact of vaccinating 18+ only versus expanding to 12+ adolescents during two different epidemic periods: late 2021 with a large Omicron wave and 2022 when the epidemic was at an endemic stage.
analysis.methods: The study used the Covasim SARS-CoV-2 model to simulate the effects of varying vaccine uptake and onset times, projecting the number of new daily infections, hospitalisations, and deaths under different vaccination strategies.
analysis.main_results: During the BA.1 Omicron wave in late 2021, expanded adolescent vaccination averted 3,000,000 cases across all ages and 1,010,000 infections in the vaccinated cohort within 2-6 months. In 2022, when the Omicron epidemic was at an endemic stage, additional adolescent vaccination did not significantly reduce the overall burden of COVID-19 or within the vaccinated cohort.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that the effectiveness of adolescent vaccination depends on the timing and speed of implementation, alongside other interventions and the epidemic status, and emphasized that it should not be considered as a standalone strategy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that public health strategies for adolescent vaccination should be tailored to the current epidemic status, incidence, and prevalence, ensuring optimal impact during periods of high transmission.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on mathematical modelling, which may not fully capture real-world complexities, and the results are specific to England's context, limiting generalisability. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the impact of adolescent vaccination against SARS-CoV-2 during two distinct epidemic phases: the Omicron wave in late 2021 and its endemic stage in 2022. Using the Covasim model, it compares vaccinating 18+ only versus expanding to 12+ adolescents. Results show that expanded vaccination significantly reduced infections during the 2021 wave but had little effect in 2022 when the epidemic was endemic. The authors conclude that adolescent vaccination effectiveness depends on implementation timing and epidemic status, and it should not be used as a standalone strategy. The study highlights the importance of aligning vaccination programs with current epidemic dynamics. However, the findings are based on mathematical models and are specific to England, limiting their generalisability and evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估青少年 疫苗接种 对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的影响如何根据流行状况而变化,特别是在 2021 年末的 Omicron 浪潮和 2022 年的流行阶段。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 英格兰使用 Covasim 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 模型进行的一项数学模型研究评估了两个不同流行时期仅为 18 岁以上青少年接种疫苗与扩大到 12 岁以上青少年的影响:2021 年末出现大规模 Omicron 波,2022 年疫情处于流行阶段。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究使用 Covasim 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 模型来模拟不同 疫苗 摄取和发病时间的影响,预测不同 疫苗 策略下每日新感染、住院和死亡的数量。
elements_zh.main_results: During the BA.1 Omicron wave in late 2021, expanded adolescent vaccination averted 3,000,000 cases across all ages and 1,010,000 infections in the vaccinated cohort within 2-6 months. In 2022, when the Omicron epidemic was at an endemic stage, additional adolescent vaccination did not significantly reduce the overall burden of COVID-19 or within the vaccinated cohort.
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,青少年 疫苗接种 的有效性取决于实施的时机和速度,以及其他干预措施和流行状况,并强调不应将其视为独立策略。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,针对青少年 疫苗接种 的公共卫生策略应根据当前的流行状况、发病率 和 患病率 进行调整,确保在高 传播 期间产生最佳影响。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于数学模型,可能无法完全捕捉现实世界的复杂性,而且结果仅针对英格兰的情况,限制了普遍性。由于这些因素,证据的强度中等。

papers.title_zh: The impact of expanded adolescent vaccination against COVID-19 depends on the epidemic status: a mathematical modelling study
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background/ObjectivesWe evaluated the impact of the COVID-19 adolescent vaccination in England at two different epidemic points: the autumn (August-November) 2021, in the presence of a large Omicron epidemic wave, and the autumn (August-November) 2022, when the subsequent Omicron epidemic was at an endemic stage. MethodsUsing the Covasim SARS-CoV-2 model for England, under varying vaccine uptake and onset time, we evaluated the impact of a)vaccinating 18+ only versus additional 12+ vaccination from the autumn 2021; and b)the current immunisation strategy at the time versus additional 12+ vaccination from September 2022, projecting the number of new daily SARS-CoV-2 infections, hospitalisations and deaths. ResultsIn presence of the BA.1 Omicron wave in late 2021, the expanded adolescent vaccination averted 3,000,000 cases across all-ages, 1,010,000 SARS-CoV-2 infections in the period 2-6 months from vaccine onset in the vaccinated cohort. During the Omicron waves in 2022, additional adolescents vaccination did not significantly reduce the COVID-19 burden in the entire population, nor within the vaccinated cohort. ConclusionsOur findings highlight that adolescent vaccination impact depends on the timing/speed of implementation, other present intervention strategies, and the status of the epidemic at the time and it should not be considered as a stand-alone immunisation strategy. HighlightsO_LIFirst study to compare the impact of expanding adolescent COVID-19 vaccination at two different epidemic points: one when a large epidemic is spreading and another at a more endemic stage of the epidemic. C_LIO_LIIn autumn 2021, in the presence of the newly emerging Omicron variant, adolescent vaccination was necessary to curb infections in both the adolescent cohort and the overall population. C_LIO_LIEarlier implementation at sufficient coverage was more effective in reducing the number of infections at the peak of the Omicron wave, and getting ahead of the epidemic spread. C_LIO_LIIn autumn 2022, when the Omicron epidemic was at an endemic stage, adolescent vaccination was not necessary to curb infections in both the adolescent cohort and the overall population. papers.title: Health-related quality of life among patients with long COVID according to the presence of a diagnosis of functional somatic disorder: A cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Long COVID is associated with poor health-related quality of life (QoL), with substantial interindividual variations. This study aimed to investigate the association between QoL and a diagnosis of functional somatic disorder (FSD) among patients seeking care for long COVID. METHODS: Data were drawn from the CASPer-COVID program, a multidisciplinary tertiary care program for patients with persistent symptoms following COVID-19. QoL was evaluated with the 36-Item Short-Form health survey (SF-36), yielding a Physical Component Summary (PCS) and a Mental Component Summary (MCS). Multivariable linear regression analyses were performed to investigate the associations between PCS or MCS scores and a diagnosis of FSD, adjusting for age, gender, body mass index, comorbidities, hospitalization for acute COVID-19, core persistent symptoms, symptom duration, depressive and anxiety symptoms, and physical activity. RESULTS: The analyses included 773 patients (median age [interquartile range (IQR)]: 44 [36-55] years; 64% women). QoL was markedly impaired (median PCS [IQR]: 44 [31-60]; median MCS [IQR]: 39 [31-49]). A diagnosis of FSD (76.5% of patients) was not associated with MCS (β [95% CI]: 1.11 [-1.30, 3.53]) or PCS (β [95% CI]: -1.60 [-3.88, 0.67]) scores in adjusted analyses. Lower PCS and MCS scores were associated with higher depressive and anxiety symptoms, lower physical activity levels, and pain. In addition, lower PCS scores were associated with female gender, hospitalization for acute COVID-19 and longer symptom duration. CONCLUSION: In patients seeking care for long COVID in a tertiary care setting, QoL did not differ significantly between those diagnosed with FSD and other patients.

analysis.scope_and_question: The study examines the association between health-related quality of life (QoL) and a diagnosis of functional somatic disorder (FSD) among patients with long COVID, focusing on the SARS-CoV-2-related condition post-COVID condition (long COVID). The central question is whether FSD diagnosis correlates with impaired physical (PCS) or mental (MCS) component summary scores of QoL in this population.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The evidence is derived from a cross-sectional analysis within the CASPer-COVID program, a multidisciplinary tertiary care initiative for patients with persistent symptoms following COVID-19. QoL was measured using the SF-36 instrument, generating PCS and MCS scores. Multivariable linear regression models adjusted for demographic, clinical, and psychological covariates to assess associations between QoL and FSD diagnosis.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Among 773 patients with long COVID, QoL was markedly impaired, with median PCS and MCS scores of 44 and 39, respectively. No significant association was found between FSD diagnosis and either PCS (β [95% CI]: -1.60 [-3.88, 0.67]) or MCS (β [95% CI]: 1.11 [-1.30, 3.53]) scores after adjustment for confounders.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study did not evaluate the temporal dynamics of QoL changes or the impact of FSD diagnosis over time. Additionally, the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference regarding the relationship between FSD and QoL in long COVID. The sample was drawn from a tertiary care setting, limiting generalizability to broader populations with long COVID.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should prioritize longitudinal studies to clarify the temporal relationship between FSD and QoL in long COVID. Investigations into the mechanisms underlying QoL impairment, particularly the roles of depressive symptoms, physical activity, and pain, are warranted. Clinically, routine screening for depressive and anxiety symptoms, as well as physical activity levels, may help identify patients at higher risk of impaired QoL.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study within the CASPer-COVID program assessed health-related quality of life (QoL) in 773 patients with long COVID, using SF-36 to derive Physical (PCS) and Mental (MCS) Component Summary scores. QoL was significantly impaired, with median PCS and MCS scores of 44 and 39, respectively. After adjusting for age, gender, comorbidities, hospitalization, symptom duration, depressive and anxiety symptoms, and physical activity, a diagnosis of functional somatic disorder (FSD) was not associated with differences in PCS or MCS scores. Lower QoL scores were linked to higher depressive and anxiety symptoms, reduced physical activity, and pain, while lower PCS scores were also associated with female gender, hospitalization for acute COVID-19, and longer symptom duration. The findings highlight the need for longitudinal research to explore causal pathways and inform targeted interventions for QoL improvement in long COVID.

analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 未来的研究应优先考虑纵向研究,以阐明 长新冠 中 FSD 和 QoL 之间的时间关系。有必要研究生活质量受损的机制,特别是抑郁症状、体力活动和疼痛的作用。临床上,对抑郁和焦虑症状以及体力活动水平进行常规筛查可能有助于识别生活质量受损风险较高的患者。

papers.title: A structural and mechanistic atlas of NTD antibody neutralization and immune escape across SARS-CoV-2 prototype and its (sub-)variants.
papers.abstract: The N-terminal domain (NTD) of the SARS-CoV-2 spike (S) is a critical antibody target, yet its epitope organization, neutralization mechanisms, and immune evasion strategies remain incompletely resolved. Here, we classify NTD antibodies into nine spatially distinct classes (designated as NTD-1 to NTD-9), including a cryptic epitope defined here (NTD-8). Mechanistic studies reveal that NTD-5 and NTD-9 antibodies neutralize by inducing S1 shedding, thereby extending this mechanism to selected NTD-directed antibodies. Format profiling shows that while most NTD antibodies require bivalency, selected antibodies from NTD-3, NTD-5, and NTD-9 retain neutralizing activity in Fab form. Profiling 41 antibodies across prototype, Delta, and 17 Omicron subvariants defines an epitope-resolved escape landscape and enables dissection of three convergent evasion strategies: contact residue disruption, glycan shielding, and conformational remodeling. Notably, the KP.3.1.1 subvariant uses a dual escape mechanism in which ∆S31 introduces N30 glycosylation and substantially remodels the S27-R34 region, undermining recognition by both NTD-5 and NTD-9 antibodies. These findings provide a structural and mechanistic framework for rational vaccine and antibody design resilient to antigenic drift.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the incomplete understanding of how antibodies targeting the N-terminal domain (NTD) of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein neutralize the virus and how immune escape occurs across variants. It asks whether the epitope organization and neutralization mechanisms of NTD antibodies can be systematically classified and mechanistically explained to inform vaccine and antibody design.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research classifies NTD antibodies into nine spatially distinct classes and profiles 41 antibodies across the SARS-CoV-2 prototype, Delta, and 17 Omicron subvariants. It includes mechanistic studies to dissect neutralization and escape strategies.
analysis.methods: Antibody classes were defined by spatial epitope mapping, and neutralization mechanisms were investigated through structural and functional assays. Escape landscapes were profiled by assessing antibody recognition across variants, including the KP.3.1.1 subvariant.
analysis.main_results: Nine NTD antibody classes (NTD-1 to NTD-9) were identified, including a cryptic epitope (NTD-8). NTD-5 and NTD-9 antibodies neutralize by inducing S1 shedding, and selected antibodies from NTD-3, NTD-5, and NTD-9 retain activity in Fab form. The KP.3.1.1 subvariant employs dual escape via ∆S31 introducing N30 glycosylation and remodeling the S27-R34 region, undermining NTD-5 and NTD-9 recognition.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The work provides an epitope-resolved escape landscape and reveals three convergent evasion strategies: contact residue disruption, glycan shielding, and conformational remodeling. It introduces a structural and mechanistic framework for designing vaccines and antibodies resilient to antigenic drift.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can guide the development of next-generation vaccines and monoclonal antibodies with improved resilience to SARS-CoV-2 immune escape, particularly against Omicron subvariants.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to structural and functional profiling in vitro and does not address in vivo efficacy, clinical outcomes, or population-level immune responses. The strength of evidence is moderate due to the abstract-only scope and lack of direct clinical validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study classifies SARS-CoV-2 N-terminal domain (NTD) antibodies into nine spatially distinct classes and profiles 41 antibodies across prototype, Delta, and 17 Omicron subvariants. Mechanistic analyses reveal that NTD-5 and NTD-9 antibodies neutralize by inducing S1 shedding, while selected antibodies retain activity in Fab form. The KP.3.1.1 subvariant escapes neutralization via dual mechanisms: introducing N30 glycosylation and remodeling the S27-R34 region, disrupting recognition by NTD-5 and NTD-9 antibodies. The work defines an epitope-resolved escape landscape and identifies three convergent evasion strategies—contact residue disruption, glycan shielding, and conformational remodeling—providing a structural framework for designing vaccines and antibodies resilient to antigenic drift.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了对针对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 刺突蛋白 N 端结构域 (NTD) 的抗体如何中和病毒以及跨变体如何发生免疫逃逸的不完全理解。它询问是否可以对 NTD 抗体的表位组织和中和机制进行系统分类和机械解释,为 疫苗 和抗体设计提供信息。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: The research classifies NTD antibodies into nine spatially distinct classes and profiles 41 antibodies across the 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 prototype,Delta,and 17 Omicron subvariants.它包括剖析中和和逃避策略的机制研究。
elements_zh.methods: 通过空间表位作图定义抗体类别,并通过结构和功能测定研究中和机制。通过评估跨变体(包括 KP.3.1.1 亚变体)的抗体识别来描绘逃逸景观。
elements_zh.main_results: 鉴定出九种 NTD 抗体类别(NTD-1 至 NTD-9),包括一个隐藏表位 (NTD-8)。NTD-5 和 NTD-9 抗体通过诱导 S1 脱落来中和,并且来自 NTD-3、NTD-5 和 NTD-9 的选定抗体以 Fab 形式保留活性。KP.3.1.1 亚变体通过 ΔS31 采用双重逃逸,引入 N30 糖基化并重塑 S27-R34 区域,破坏 NTD-5 和 NTD-9 识别。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: The work provides an epitope-resolved escape landscape and reveals three convergent evasion strategies: contact residue disruption,glycan shielding,and conformational remodeling.它介绍了用于设计 疫苗 和抗抗原漂移的抗体的结构和机制框架。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以指导下一代 疫苗 和单克隆抗体的开发,这些抗体具有更高的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 免疫逃逸恢复能力,特别是针对 Omicron 亚变体。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于体外结构和功能分析,不涉及体内功效、临床结果或群体水平 免疫应答。由于仅限摘要范围且缺乏直接的临床验证,证据强度中等。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了对针对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 刺突蛋白 N 端结构域 (NTD) 的抗体如何中和病毒以及跨变体如何发生免疫逃逸的不完全理解。它询问是否可以对 NTD 抗体的表位组织和中和机制进行系统分类和机械解释,为 疫苗 和抗体设计提供信息。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: The research classifies NTD antibodies into nine spatially distinct classes and profiles 41 antibodies across the 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 prototype,Delta,and 17 Omicron subvariants.它包括剖析中和和逃避策略的机制研究。
analysis_zh.methods: 通过空间表位作图定义抗体类别,并通过结构和功能测定研究中和机制。通过评估跨变体(包括 KP.3.1.1 亚变体)的抗体识别来描绘逃逸景观。
analysis_zh.main_results: 鉴定出九种 NTD 抗体类别(NTD-1 至 NTD-9),包括一个隐藏表位 (NTD-8)。NTD-5 和 NTD-9 抗体通过诱导 S1 脱落来中和,并且来自 NTD-3、NTD-5 和 NTD-9 的选定抗体以 Fab 形式保留活性。KP.3.1.1 亚变体通过 ΔS31 采用双重逃逸,引入 N30 糖基化并重塑 S27-R34 区域,破坏 NTD-5 和 NTD-9 识别。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: The work provides an epitope-resolved escape landscape and reveals three convergent evasion strategies: contact residue disruption,glycan shielding,and conformational remodeling.它介绍了用于设计 疫苗 和抗抗原漂移的抗体的结构和机制框架。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以指导下一代 疫苗 和单克隆抗体的开发,这些抗体具有更高的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 免疫逃逸恢复能力,特别是针对 Omicron 亚变体。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于体外结构和功能分析,不涉及体内功效、临床结果或群体水平 免疫应答。由于仅限摘要范围且缺乏直接的临床验证,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Seroprevalence convergence masks persistent socioeconomic disparities in SARS-CoV-2 infection risk in Canada
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Socioeconomic disparities in COVID-19 outcomes have been widely documented, but evidence regarding inequities in SARS-CoV-2 infection risk remains mixed. In Canada, infection-induced seroprevalence appeared to converge across socioeconomic strata by late 2022, raising questions about whether inequities in infection risk diminished during the Omicron period. AIM: To assess whether apparent convergence in SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence reflects true equity in infection risk or masks persistent socioeconomic disparities in force of infection. METHODS: We analysed serial cross-sectional SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence data (anti-nucleocapsid antibodies) from Canadian Blood Services donors collected between April 2021 and April 2023 and stratified by area-level material deprivation quintile (Q1 = least deprived; Q5 = most deprived). We fitted a dynamic seronegative-seropositive model with sero-reversion to the full seroprevalence time series, estimating quintile-specific forces of infection before and after the emergence of the Omicron variant (January 2022). Models allowing differential Omicron-related amplification by material deprivation were compared using likelihood-based criteria. RESULTS: During the pre-Omicron period, the most deprived quintile (Q5) experienced a 71% higher force of infection than the least deprived (Q1; incidence rate ratio (IRR): 1.71; 95% CI: 1.60-1.83). Following Omicron emergence, force of infection rose markedly in all quintiles. Because the pre-Omicron baseline was lowest in the least-deprived quintile, the relative increase during Omicron was largest there (48.5-fold) and smallest in the most-deprived quintile (31.8-fold), compressing the relative socioeconomic gradient (Q5 vs Q1 IRR: 1.12; 95% CI: 1.11-1.14). Despite this compression in relative terms, the most deprived populations continued to experience higher absolute force of infection throughout the Omicron period. CONCLUSION: Convergence in SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence across socioeconomic strata masked persistent inequalities in force of infection. Dynamic modelling demonstrates that apparent equity is attributable, in our modelling framework, to differential amplification of force of infection during the Omicron period rather than from elimination of underlying socioeconomic disparities.

analysis.study_design_and_population: This study analysed serial cross-sectional SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence data from Canadian Blood Services donors collected between April 2021 and April 2023, stratified by area-level material deprivation quintile (Q1 = least deprived; Q5 = most deprived).
analysis.methods: Seroprevalence was measured using anti-nucleocapsid antibody assays. A dynamic seronegative-seropositive model with sero-reversion was fitted to the full seroprevalence time series to estimate quintile-specific forces of infection before and after the emergence of the Omicron variant (January 2022). Models allowing differential Omicron-related amplification by material deprivation were compared using likelihood-based criteria.
analysis.main_results: During the pre-Omicron period, the most deprived quintile (Q5) experienced a 71% higher force of infection than the least deprived (Q1; incidence rate ratio (IRR): 1.71; 95% CI: 1.60–1.83). Following Omicron emergence, the relative increase in force of infection was largest in the least-deprived quintile (48.5-fold) and smallest in the most-deprived quintile (31.8-fold), compressing the relative socioeconomic gradient (Q5 vs Q1 IRR: 1.12; 95% CI: 1.11–1.14). Despite this compression, the most deprived populations continued to experience higher absolute force of infection throughout the Omicron period.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the convergence in seroprevalence as masking persistent socioeconomic inequalities in force of infection, attributing this to differential amplification of infection risk during the Omicron period rather than elimination of underlying disparities. This study provides novel evidence that relative seroprevalence convergence can obscure ongoing inequities in absolute infection risk.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings caution against interpreting seroprevalence convergence as evidence of reduced infection risk disparities and highlight the need for targeted surveillance and prevention strategies in socioeconomically deprived populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on area-level deprivation measures and donor-based seroprevalence data, which may not fully capture individual-level socioeconomic factors or infection histories. The evidence strength is moderate due to model dependence and potential biases inherent in sero-reversion assumptions and sampling frames.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated whether apparent convergence in SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence across socioeconomic strata in Canada reflected true equity in infection risk or masked persistent disparities. Using serial cross-sectional seroprevalence data from Canadian Blood Services donors (April 2021–April 2023) stratified by material deprivation quintile, the authors fitted a dynamic seronegative-seropositive model to estimate forces of infection before and after Omicron emergence. Pre-Omicron, the most deprived quintile had a 71% higher force of infection than the least deprived (IRR 1.71; 95% CI 1.60–1.83). During Omicron, relative increases were largest in the least-deprived quintile (48.5-fold) and smallest in the most-deprived (31.8-fold), compressing the relative gradient (IRR 1.12; 95% CI 1.11–1.14), yet absolute risk remained higher in deprived groups. The authors conclude that seroprevalence convergence masked persistent inequities, driven by differential Omicron amplification rather than elimination of disparities. These findings underscore the risk of misinterpreting seroprevalence trends and support targeted public health interventions in socioeconomically vulnerable populations.

elements_zh.main_results: 在 Omicron 之前的时期,最贫困的五分之一 (Q5) 的感染力比最贫困的五分之一 (Q1;发病率 率比 (IRR):1.71;95% CI:1.60–1.83)高 71%。Omicron 出现后,感染力的相对增幅在最贫困的五分之一中最大(48.5 倍),在最贫困的五分之一中最小(31.8 倍),压缩了相对社会经济梯度(Q5 与 Q1 IRR:1.12;95% CI:1.11-1.14)。尽管存在这种压缩,但在整个 Omicron 时期,最贫困的人群继续经历着更高的绝对感染力。

papers.title_zh: 血清流行率 趋同掩盖了加拿大 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染风险中持续存在的社会经济差异
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Socioeconomic disparities in COVID-19 outcomes have been widely documented, but evidence regarding inequities in SARS-CoV-2 infection risk remains mixed. In Canada, infection-induced seroprevalence appeared to converge across socioeconomic strata by late 2022, raising questions about whether inequities in infection risk diminished during the Omicron period. AIM: To assess whether apparent convergence in SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence reflects true equity in infection risk or masks persistent socioeconomic disparities in force of infection. METHODS: We analysed serial cross-sectional SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence data (anti-nucleocapsid antibodies) from Canadian Blood Services donors collected between April 2021 and April 2023 and stratified by area-level material deprivation quintile (Q1 = least deprived; Q5 = most deprived). We fitted a dynamic seronegative-seropositive model with sero-reversion to the full seroprevalence time series, estimating quintile-specific forces of infection before and after the emergence of the Omicron variant (January 2022). Models allowing differential Omicron-related amplification by material deprivation were compared using likelihood-based criteria. RESULTS: During the pre-Omicron period, the most deprived quintile (Q5) experienced a 71% higher force of infection than the least deprived (Q1; incidence rate ratio (IRR): 1.71; 95% CI: 1.60-1.83). Following Omicron emergence, force of infection rose markedly in all quintiles. Because the pre-Omicron baseline was lowest in the least-deprived quintile, the relative increase during Omicron was largest there (48.5-fold) and smallest in the most-deprived quintile (31.8-fold), compressing the relative socioeconomic gradient (Q5 vs Q1 IRR: 1.12; 95% CI: 1.11-1.14). Despite this compression in relative terms, the most deprived populations continued to experience higher absolute force of infection throughout the Omicron period. CONCLUSION: Convergence in SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence across socioeconomic strata masked persistent inequalities in force of infection. Dynamic modelling demonstrates that apparent equity is attributable, in our modelling framework, to differential amplification of force of infection during the Omicron period rather than from elimination of underlying socioeconomic disparities.

papers.title: Persistent humoral, cellular, and transcriptional signatures associated with protective immunity against SARS-CoV-2 observed 18-months after COVID-19 vaccinations during the Omicron wave in Pakistan
papers.abstract: Abstract During the COVID-19 pandemic the population experienced waves of SARS-CoV-2 infections as well as vaccinations. Concern with longer term effectiveness of vaccinations led to booster vaccinations across global population, more high resource settings but not in low middle income countries such as Pakistan. We studied a population which received different COVID-19 vaccines (inactivated, mRNA and vector types) and were tested this one year and a half afterwards. Humoral responses determined through IgG antibody levels and cellular immunity studied through T cell reactivity to SARS-CoV-2 antigens all indicated persistent protection against the coronavirus. Through a comparison with a pre-pandemic cohort, host blood transcriptional profiles of the post-vaccination cohort showed upregulated cellular signaling and protein synthesis pathways reflective of vaccine associated changes. Additionally, cellular stress associated responses were apparent which are consistent with viral infection signatures as well as vaccination effects. Our results reflect an effect likely as a combination of COVID-19 vaccination and immune boosting due to SARS-CoV-2 transmission leading to trained immunity in the absence of COVID-19 boosters. It’s the first work of its kind- very limited information globally on post-pandemic immunity. It shows at the transcriptional level how immune activation is maintained, stress pathways and cellular senescence. These data show hybrid immunity likely gave longer-term protection observed in Pakistan despite limited COVID-19 vaccination availability, with relatively low morbidity and mortality.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed concerns about the durability of vaccine-induced immunity against SARS-CoV-2, particularly in low- and middle-income countries such as Pakistan where booster availability was limited during the Omicron wave.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research examined a population in Pakistan that had received different COVID-19 vaccines (inactivated, mRNA, and vector types) and evaluated immune responses approximately 18 months after vaccination.
analysis.methods: The study assessed humoral immunity via IgG antibody levels and cellular immunity through T cell reactivity to SARS-CoV-2 antigens, alongside host blood transcriptional profiling to identify pathway changes associated with vaccine responses.
analysis.main_results: Humoral and cellular immune responses indicated persistent protection against SARS-CoV-2, and transcriptional profiles showed upregulated cellular signaling and protein synthesis pathways consistent with vaccine-associated changes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as evidence that hybrid immunity—combining vaccination and natural infection—likely contributed to sustained protection in Pakistan despite limited booster availability, and noted this was among the first studies to characterize post-pandemic immunity at the transcriptional level.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that hybrid immunity may have provided longer-term protection in low-resource settings, potentially informing vaccination strategies and surveillance approaches in similar contexts.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to abstract-level data and lacks detailed methodological, demographic, or statistical reporting, which constrains the strength of the conclusions and generalizability.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the durability of vaccine-induced immunity against SARS-CoV-2 in a Pakistani population 18 months after receiving different COVID-19 vaccines during the Omicron wave. Using humoral, cellular, and transcriptional profiling, the authors observed persistent immune responses and upregulated cellular pathways indicative of vaccine-associated changes. They interpreted these findings as evidence that hybrid immunity—from vaccination and natural infection—likely sustained protection despite limited booster availability. The work is notable for being among the first to characterize post-pandemic immunity at the transcriptional level. However, the evidence is restricted to abstract-level data, limiting the strength and generalizability of the conclusions.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: The study addressed concerns about the durability of vaccine-induced immunity against SARS-CoV-2, particularly in low- and middle-income countries such as Pakistan where booster availability was limited during the Omicron wave.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: The research examined a population in Pakistan that had received different COVID-19 vaccines (inactivated, mRNA, and vector types) and evaluated immune responses approximately 18 months after vaccination.
elements_en.methods: The study assessed humoral immunity via IgG antibody levels and cellular immunity through T cell reactivity to SARS-CoV-2 antigens, alongside host blood transcriptional profiling to identify pathway changes associated with vaccine responses.
elements_en.main_results: Humoral and cellular immune responses indicated persistent protection against SARS-CoV-2, and transcriptional profiles showed upregulated cellular signaling and protein synthesis pathways consistent with vaccine-associated changes.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as evidence that hybrid immunity—combining vaccination and natural infection—likely contributed to sustained protection in Pakistan despite limited booster availability, and noted this was among the first studies to characterize post-pandemic immunity at the transcriptional level.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that hybrid immunity may have provided longer-term protection in low-resource settings, potentially informing vaccination strategies and surveillance approaches in similar contexts.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to abstract-level data and lacks detailed methodological, demographic, or statistical reporting, which constrains the strength of the conclusions and generalizability.

papers.title_zh: Persistent humoral, cellular, and transcriptional signatures associated with protective immunity against SARS-CoV-2 observed 18-months after COVID-19 vaccinations during the Omicron wave in Pakistan
papers.source_body_en: Abstract During the COVID-19 pandemic the population experienced waves of SARS-CoV-2 infections as well as vaccinations. Concern with longer term effectiveness of vaccinations led to booster vaccinations across global population, more high resource settings but not in low middle income countries such as Pakistan. We studied a population which received different COVID-19 vaccines (inactivated, mRNA and vector types) and were tested this one year and a half afterwards. Humoral responses determined through IgG antibody levels and cellular immunity studied through T cell reactivity to SARS-CoV-2 antigens all indicated persistent protection against the coronavirus. Through a comparison with a pre-pandemic cohort, host blood transcriptional profiles of the post-vaccination cohort showed upregulated cellular signaling and protein synthesis pathways reflective of vaccine associated changes. Additionally, cellular stress associated responses were apparent which are consistent with viral infection signatures as well as vaccination effects. Our results reflect an effect likely as a combination of COVID-19 vaccination and immune boosting due to SARS-CoV-2 transmission leading to trained immunity in the absence of COVID-19 boosters. It’s the first work of its kind- very limited information globally on post-pandemic immunity. It shows at the transcriptional level how immune activation is maintained, stress pathways and cellular senescence. These data show hybrid immunity likely gave longer-term protection observed in Pakistan despite limited COVID-19 vaccination availability, with relatively low morbidity and mortality.

papers.title: Healthy vaccinee effect in the evaluation of updated COVID-19 vaccines in elderly populations
papers.abstract: Abstract Established determinants of health in the elderly help guide routines for indicated vaccine administration, while unmeasured frailty may limit vaccine access. We evaluate the performance of the 2024-2025 COVID-19 vaccine adapted to the Omicron JN.1 lineage in a Swedish population aged ≥65 years ( N = 245 696). Vaccine effectiveness (VE) on COVID-19-related hospitalization and a negative control outcome (NCO; all-cause mortality) are assessed in various cohorts between October 1, 2024 to March 31, 2025. The VE was 75% (95% CI 70%–79%) overall, and 84% (95% CI 80%–87%) and 65% (95% CI 34%–82%) in individuals with and without vaccination with the prior updated COVID-19 vaccine in 2023-2024, respectively. The NCO in individuals exposed to the study vaccine in 2024-2025 was half of that seen in those not exposed to the vaccine (HR 0.43 [95% CI 0.40–0.45]). Removing individuals hospitalized with COVID-19 from this population did not change the difference in NCO (HR 0.43 [95% CI 0.41-0.46]). These findings suggest the presence of selection effects arising from under-provision of health services to elderly individuals with frailty. The healthy vaccinee effect should be considered in observational studies of the effectiveness of updated COVID-19 vaccines in elderly populations.
