analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses whether updated COVID-19 vaccines adapted to the Omicron JN.1 lineage provide protection against hospitalization in elderly populations, where unmeasured frailty may bias vaccine effectiveness estimates.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cohort study was conducted in Sweden among individuals aged 65 years or older (N = 245,696) between October 1, 2024, and March 31, 2025, to evaluate vaccine effectiveness against COVID-19-related hospitalization.
analysis.methods: Vaccine effectiveness was assessed using observational cohorts, with a negative control outcome (all-cause mortality) to detect healthy vaccinee effects, and hazard ratios were calculated to compare outcomes between vaccinated and unvaccinated groups.
analysis.main_results: The vaccine effectiveness was 75% (95% CI 70%–79%) overall, with higher effectiveness in individuals previously vaccinated in 2023–2024 (84%, 95% CI 80%–87%) compared to those without prior vaccination (65%, 95% CI 34%–82%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as evidence of selection effects due to under-provision of health services to frail elderly individuals, highlighting the need to account for the healthy vaccinee effect in observational vaccine effectiveness studies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that updated COVID-19 vaccines remain effective in preventing hospitalization in elderly populations but may overestimate protection if frailty-related access disparities are not addressed in surveillance.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its observational design, potential residual confounding from unmeasured frailty, and reliance on administrative data, which may affect the accuracy of vaccine effectiveness estimates and generalizability.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the effectiveness of the 2024–2025 Omicron JN.1-adapted COVID-19 vaccine in preventing hospitalization among Swedish adults aged 65 years or older. Using a cohort design, the authors estimated an overall vaccine effectiveness of 75% (95% CI 70%–79%), with higher protection observed in individuals previously vaccinated (84%) compared to those without prior vaccination (65%). A negative control outcome analysis revealed a healthy vaccinee effect, as vaccinated individuals had half the hazard of all-cause mortality compared to unvaccinated individuals (HR 0.43, 95% CI 0.40–0.45), even after excluding those hospitalized with COVID-19. The authors attribute these findings to selection bias arising from under-provision of health services to frail elderly individuals. While the results support the continued use of updated vaccines in this population, the observational design and potential confounding limit causal inference and generalizability.

papers.title: Epidemiology and mortality among hospital-acquired cases of COVID-19 in the pre-Omicron and Omicron periods: A data-linkage study in Victoria, Australia.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to compare the epidemiology and mortality of hospital-acquired versus non-hospital-acquired COVID-19 infections among hospitalised patients. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of COVID‐19 hospitalisations in Victoria, Australia (January 2021-June 2024), using linked state surveillance systems. Episodes were classified as hospital acquired if the first positive test occurred ≥8 days post admission. Age, sex, intensive care unit admission and 30‐day mortality were compared between hospital-acquired and non‐hospital-acquired cases across pre‐Omicron and Omicron periods. RESULTS: Of 6,485 hospital-acquired and 62,670 non-hospital-acquired episodes, median age for hospital-acquired versus non-hospital-acquired cases was 77.8 versus 77.6 years before Omicron and 52.6 versus 73.1 years during Omicron. Monthly proportion of hospital-acquired cases increased during Omicron (range: 1% to 21%). Case fatality rates were higher in hospital-acquired than in non-hospital-acquired cases, with a larger difference before the Omicron (incidence rate ratio: 4.49, 95% confidence interval: 2.02, 9.99) than during the Omicron period (incidence rate ratio: 1.62, 95% confidence interval: 1.44, 1.82). papers.title: Pathogenicity of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron subvariants JN.1, EG.5.1, and BA.2.86.1 in immunologically naïve cynomolgus macaques.
papers.abstract: Since the emergence of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant, decreased morbidity and mortality relative to early strains have been widely reported. However, the virological characteristics of recent subvariants dominating the post-pandemic era remain to be fully elucidated. In the present study, the intrinsic pathogenicities of the Omicron subvariants JN.1, EG.5.1, and BA.2.86.1 were investigated using an immunologically naïve cynomolgus macaque model. All three variants exhibited robust replication in the upper respiratory tract, surpassing the viral titers observed with the early Wuhan strain. Omicron subvariant infection caused prolonged fever and sustained viral shedding in the nasal mucosa for at least seven days, indicating enhanced adaptation to upper airway tissues. Despite this shift in viral replication tropism, histological analysis showed that these variants retained the characteristics to induce lower respiratory tract disease. All infected macaques developed bronchopneumonia characterized by cellular exudates in the alveolar spaces. The histological scores were comparable to those observed with the early strain. These findings demonstrate that the pathogenicity of the Omicron subvariants has not been fully attenuated in the absence of pre-existing immunity, since they caused severe lung disease in immunologically naïve macaques. Furthermore, their enhanced propagation in the upper airway likely facilitates efficient transmission among humans. The continuous circulation of SARS-CoV-2 variants underscores the necessity of ongoing surveillance of viral gene variations and the maintenance of protective immunity in vulnerable populations.

In the present study, the intrinsic pathogenicities of the Omicron subvariants JN.1, EG.5.1, and BA.2.86.1 were investigated using an immunologically naïve cynomolgus macaque model. All three variants exhibited robust replication in the upper respiratory tract, surpassing the viral titers observed with the early Wuhan strain. Omicron subvariant infection caused prolonged fever and sustained viral shedding in the nasal mucosa for at least seven days, indicating enhanced adaptation to upper airway tissues. Despite this shift in viral replication tropism, histological analysis showed that these variants retained the characteristics to induce lower respiratory tract disease. All infected macaques developed bronchopneumonia characterized by cellular exudates in the alveolar spaces. The histological scores were comparable to those observed with the early strain. These findings demonstrate that the pathogenicity of the Omicron subvariants has not been fully attenuated in the absence of pre-existing immunity, since they caused severe lung disease in immunologically naïve macaques. Furthermore, their enhanced propagation in the upper airway likely facilitates efficient transmission among humans. The continuous circulation of SARS-CoV-2 variants underscores the necessity of ongoing surveillance of viral gene variations and the maintenance of protective immunity in vulnerable populations.

papers.abstract_zh: 自从 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Omicron 变种出现以来,相对于早期菌株的发病率降低和 死亡率 已被广泛报道。然而,在大流行后时代占主导地位的近期亚变体的病毒学特征仍有待充分阐明。在本研究中,使用免疫学幼稚的食蟹猴模型研究了 Omicron 亚变体 JN.1、EG.5.1 和 BA.2.86.1 的内在致病性。所有三种变体都在上呼吸道中表现出强劲的复制能力,超过了早期武汉病毒株观察到的病毒滴度。Omicron 亚变体感染导致长时间发烧,并在鼻粘膜中持续病毒脱落至少 7 天,表明对上呼吸道组织的适应增强。尽管病毒复制向性发生了这种转变,但组织学分析表明这些变异体保留了诱发下呼吸道疾病的特征。所有受感染的猕猴都会出现支气管肺炎,其特征是肺泡腔内有细胞渗出物。组织学评分与早期菌株观察到的组织学评分相当。这些发现表明,在缺乏预先存在的免疫力的情况下,Omicron 亚变体的致病性并未完全减弱,因为它们在免疫学上未接触过的猕猴中引起了严重的肺部疾病。此外,它们在上呼吸道的增强传播可能有助于人类中有效的 传播。严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变种的持续传播强调了持续监测病毒基因变异和维持易感人群保护性免疫力的必要性。

papers.title: Clinical outcomes of neurosurgical patients during the COVID-19 pandemic: a systematic review and meta-analysis of global data.
papers.abstract: Background COVID-19 pandemic has substantially affected neurosurgical care globally through service reorganizations, delayed presentation, alterations in case selection, and limited perioperative resources. However, overall impact of these changes on clinical outcomes in neurosurgical patients remains unclear. Hence, this review evaluated clinical outcomes of neurosurgical patients managed during COVID-19 era compared with pre-pandemic era. Methods Systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science was conducted from inception of database till March 2026. Pooled effect estimates were calculated using random-effects meta-analysis. Odds ratios (ORs) were used for dichotomous outcomes and weighted mean differences (WMDs) for continuous outcomes. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 statistic. Results Twenty studies were included. In the primary pre-pandemic comparison, mortality was significantly higher during the COVID-19 era across 18 studies including 35,639 patients (OR = 1.49, 95%CI 1.20-1.85; I2 = 44.7%). Postoperative complications were also increased across 13 studies including 12,174 patients (OR = 1.44, 95%CI 1.04-1.98; I2 = 78.5%). No significant difference was observed for requirement of mechanical ventilation (OR = 1.20, 95%CI 0.81-1.76; I2 = 0.0%), whereas length-of-stay findings were inconclusive because of high heterogeneity (WMD = -1.46 days, 95%CI -3.19 to 0.28; I2 = 85.8%). Conclusions Neurosurgical patients managed during the COVID-19 era had higher mortality and postoperative complication rates than those treated before the pandemic. These findings highlight the vulnerability of neurosurgical care systems to large-scale health-system disruption and underscore the need for resilient strategies to ensure timely and safer neurosurgical care during future disruptions. Clinical trial registration Not applicable.

papers.title_zh: Clinical outcomes of neurosurgical patients during the COVID-19 pandemic: a systematic review and meta-analysis of global data.
papers.source_body_en: Background COVID-19 pandemic has substantially affected neurosurgical care globally through service reorganizations, delayed presentation, alterations in case selection, and limited perioperative resources. However, overall impact of these changes on clinical outcomes in neurosurgical patients remains unclear. Hence, this review evaluated clinical outcomes of neurosurgical patients managed during COVID-19 era compared with pre-pandemic era. Methods Systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science was conducted from inception of database till March 2026. Pooled effect estimates were calculated using random-effects meta-analysis. Odds ratios (ORs) were used for dichotomous outcomes and weighted mean differences (WMDs) for continuous outcomes. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 statistic. Results Twenty studies were included. In the primary pre-pandemic comparison, mortality was significantly higher during the COVID-19 era across 18 studies including 35,639 patients (OR = 1.49, 95%CI 1.20-1.85; I2 = 44.7%). Postoperative complications were also increased across 13 studies including 12,174 patients (OR = 1.44, 95%CI 1.04-1.98; I2 = 78.5%). No significant difference was observed for requirement of mechanical ventilation (OR = 1.20, 95%CI 0.81-1.76; I2 = 0.0%), whereas length-of-stay findings were inconclusive because of high heterogeneity (WMD = -1.46 days, 95%CI -3.19 to 0.28; I2 = 85.8%). Conclusions Neurosurgical patients managed during the COVID-19 era had higher mortality and postoperative complication rates than those treated before the pandemic. These findings highlight the vulnerability of neurosurgical care systems to large-scale health-system disruption and underscore the need for resilient strategies to ensure timely and safer neurosurgical care during future disruptions. papers.title: Ethnic reporting and representation in UK COVID-19 consenting observational studies; a systematic review
papers.abstract: Background Evidence suggests ethnic minority populations are disproportionately impacted by COVID-19, however ethnic minority groups are often under-represented in research with ethnicity associations not being investigated. Observational studies are an important tool for understanding the health inequalities of ethnic minority populations. We aimed to assess the reporting of ethnic composition and representation of ethnic minority groups in COVID-19 consented observational studies in the UK. Methods A systematic review of COVID-19 studies was conducted in OVID MedLine electronic database (1 st January 2020-22 nd November 2022). Observational, opt-in consenting studies of COVID-19 exposures and outcomes with a minimum of 96 participants in the UK only were eligible. Studies that were non-medical, COVID-19 vaccination studies and studies investigating the impact of COVID-19 policies were excluded as were studies that registered only children (<18 years). Data analysis was conducted in R v4.3.3. Results This systematic review comprised of 138 studies of which 100 (72.5%) reported participant ethnicity, most commonly through self-reporting by participants. Only 15 of the studies reporting ethnicity (15%) used the recognised ONS ethnicity categories for reporting participant ethnicity. Studies acquired their data either through self-conducted studies or from large, observational study databases. UK-Biobank data was the most common database being used for 69 (50%) of the studies. Conclusion Reporting of participant ethnicity in consenting, observational COVID-19 studies in the UK was found to be inconsistent or missing despite early evidence of ethnic minority groups being disproportionately affected by the disease and most studies having access to, at a minimum, ONS five high-level ethnicity data through their use of large databases such as UK-Biobank. This made quantitative assessment of representation challenging. However, many studies under-represented ethnic minority participants compared to the 2021 England and Wales Census data.

papers.title: Effects of State Medicaid Expansions Affecting Parental Eligibility on Children's Healthcare Access and Health During the COVID-19 Pandemic.
papers.abstract: Objective To examine whether pre-pandemic state Medicaid expansions for adults affected children's healthcare access and utilization, child health, and parental health during the COVID-19 pandemic. Methods The sample includes children from households with incomes up to 138% of the Federal Poverty Level using data from the 2016-2023 National Survey of Children's Health. Child outcomes include insurance coverage, usual place for sick care, personal doctor or nurse, unmet healthcare needs, past 12-month utilization of any medical services, preventive medical and dental visits, mental health professional treatments, non-mental health specialist visits, emergency department visits, hospitalizations, and general/oral health ratings. Parent outcomes include physical and mental health ratings. Difference-in-differences models estimate year-by-year differences in outcomes between Medicaid expansion and non-expansion states. Results There is a decline in usual place for sick care, personal doctor or nurse, and preventive medical visits in the first or second pandemic year and in child health in 2020/2023 in expansion versus non-expansion states. In contrast, there is an increase in mental health professional treatments and other specialist visits in 2021-2023 in expansion states. Lastly, there are declines in maternal physical/mental health and father's mental health in 2020 but increase in father's mental/physical health in 2023 in expansion states. Conclusion During the pandemic, children in low-income households had less care continuity and preventive care but more mental health treatments and non-mental specialist visits in Medicaid expansion versus non-expansion states. There were also declines in both child and parent health. Findings potentially reflect intertwined effects from greater parental coverage but more pandemic-related social mobility restrictions disrupting routine/preventive care and worsening mental health more in expansion states.

analysis.methods: Difference-in-differences models were employed to estimate year-by-year differences in outcomes between Medicaid expansion and non-expansion states.
analysis.main_results: There was a decline in usual place for sick care, personal doctor or nurse, and preventive medical visits in the first or second pandemic year and in child health in 2020/2023 in expansion versus non-expansion states. In contrast, there was an increase in mental health professional treatments and other specialist visits in 2021-2023 in expansion states.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that Medicaid expansions may have had mixed effects on children's healthcare, with reduced continuity of care and preventive services but increased mental health treatments and specialist visits during the pandemic.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results highlight the complex impact of Medicaid expansions on children's healthcare access and health during the pandemic, informing future policy decisions and public health strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on observational data and difference-in-differences models, which may be subject to confounding factors and limitations in causal inference.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the effects of pre-pandemic state Medicaid expansions on children's healthcare access and health during the COVID-19 pandemic. Using data from the National Survey of Children's Health, it finds that Medicaid expansion states experienced declines in routine care and preventive services but increases in mental health treatments and specialist visits. The results suggest a complex interplay between expanded parental coverage and pandemic-related disruptions. The study's findings have implications for understanding how healthcare policies affect vulnerable populations during public health crises. However, the reliance on observational data and potential confounding factors limits the strength of causal conclusions.

papers.title_zh: Effects of State Medicaid Expansions Affecting Parental Eligibility on Children's Healthcare Access and Health During the COVID-19 Pandemic.
papers.source_body_en: Objective To examine whether pre-pandemic state Medicaid expansions for adults affected children's healthcare access and utilization, child health, and parental health during the COVID-19 pandemic. Methods The sample includes children from households with incomes up to 138% of the Federal Poverty Level using data from the 2016-2023 National Survey of Children's Health. Child outcomes include insurance coverage, usual place for sick care, personal doctor or nurse, unmet healthcare needs, past 12-month utilization of any medical services, preventive medical and dental visits, mental health professional treatments, non-mental health specialist visits, emergency department visits, hospitalizations, and general/oral health ratings. Parent outcomes include physical and mental health ratings. Difference-in-differences models estimate year-by-year differences in outcomes between Medicaid expansion and non-expansion states. Results There is a decline in usual place for sick care, personal doctor or nurse, and preventive medical visits in the first or second pandemic year and in child health in 2020/2023 in expansion versus non-expansion states. In contrast, there is an increase in mental health professional treatments and other specialist visits in 2021-2023 in expansion states. Lastly, there are declines in maternal physical/mental health and father's mental health in 2020 but increase in father's mental/physical health in 2023 in expansion states. Conclusion During the pandemic, children in low-income households had less care continuity and preventive care but more mental health treatments and non-mental specialist visits in Medicaid expansion versus non-expansion states. There were also declines in both child and parent health. Findings potentially reflect intertwined effects from greater parental coverage but more pandemic-related social mobility restrictions disrupting routine/preventive care and worsening mental health more in expansion states.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of Nucleocapsid- and Spike-Specific Isotype Humoral Immune Responses Following Natural SARS-CoV-2 Infection and Vaccination with Sinopharm, Sinovac, and AstraZeneca.
papers.abstract: The diversity of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) vaccine platforms and widespread natural exposure have created a complex landscape of humoral immunity requiring detailed characterization. Here, we compare nucleocapsid (N)- and spike (S)-specific antibody responses in sera from infected humans (IH) during the first pandemic wave (April–August 2020) and in vaccine recipients (Sinopharm, Sinovac, or AstraZeneca) using commercial ELISA kits. Among naturally IH, the IgG-positivity rate was higher for N (80.9%) than S (42.8%), with significantly elevated N-specific IgG levels compared to prepandemic controls ( p -value <0.05), while IgM responses showed no significant differences. Strong positive correlations were observed between S- and N-specific antibody responses, particularly for IgG and its subclasses. Vaccinated cohorts exhibited high IgG positivity rate (83–100%) against both antigens with low IgM levels, and overall IgG and subclass responses were significantly elevated relative to pre-pandemic controls ( p -value <0.05), with consistently strong inter-antigen correlations across groups. Overall, natural infection induces a coordinated humoral response biased toward the nucleocapsid antigen, supporting its utility as a marker of recent infection, whereas vaccination elicits a robust multi-subclass antibody response with platform-dependent differences in antigen recognition and subclass distribution.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to characterize the humoral immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid (N) and spike (S) antigens following natural infection and vaccination with different platforms, as the diversity of vaccine platforms and natural exposure has created a complex landscape of immunity requiring detailed understanding.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study compared N- and S-specific antibody responses in sera from individuals with natural SARS-CoV-2 infection during the first pandemic wave (April–August 2020) and in vaccine recipients who had been vaccinated with Sinopharm, Sinovac, or AstraZeneca.
analysis.methods: Antibody responses were measured using commercial ELISA kits to assess IgG and IgM positivity rates against N and S antigens in sera from infected humans and vaccine recipients.
analysis.main_results: Among naturally infected individuals, the IgG-positivity rate was higher for N (80.9%) than S (42.8%), with significantly elevated N-specific IgG levels compared to prepandemic controls (p-value <0.05). Vaccinated cohorts showed high IgG positivity rates (83–100%) against both antigens with low IgM levels, and overall IgG and subclass responses were significantly elevated relative to pre-pandemic controls (p-value <0.05).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that natural infection induces a coordinated humoral response biased toward the nucleocapsid antigen, whereas vaccination elicits a robust multi-subclass antibody response with platform-dependent differences in antigen recognition and subclass distribution.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results support the use of nucleocapsid-specific antibodies as a marker for recent SARS-CoV-2 infection and highlight the importance of understanding platform-dependent differences in vaccine-induced immune responses for improved surveillance and vaccine development.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to sera from the first pandemic wave and does not account for long-term immunity or variant-specific responses, but the evidence is strong due to the direct comparison of antibody responses using validated ELISA methods.

analysis.summary_en: This study compares the humoral immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid (N) and spike (S) antigens following natural infection and vaccination with Sinopharm, Sinovac, and AstraZeneca. It finds that natural infection leads to higher N-specific IgG levels compared to S-specific responses, while vaccination results in robust IgG positivity against both antigens. The study highlights platform-dependent differences in vaccine-induced antibody responses and suggests the potential utility of N-specific antibodies as a marker for recent infection. The findings are supported by commercial ELISA assays and are relevant for understanding immunity dynamics. However, the study is limited to the first pandemic wave and does not address long-term immunity or variant-specific responses, which may affect the generalizability of the results.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在表征自然感染后的体液 免疫应答 至 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 核衣壳 (N) 和刺突 (S) 抗原以及不同平台的 疫苗接种,因为 疫苗 平台和自然暴露的多样性创造了复杂的免疫景观,需要详细了解。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究比较了第一波大流行期间(2020 年 4 月至 8 月)自然 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染者的血清中的 N 和 S 特异性抗体反应,以及接种了国药集团、科兴或阿斯利康疫苗的 疫苗 接受者的血清中的 N 和 S 特异性抗体反应。
elements_zh.methods: 使用商业 ELISA 试剂盒测量抗体反应,以评估感染者和 疫苗 受体血清中 N 和 S 抗原的 IgG 和 IgM 阳性率。
elements_zh.main_results: 在自然感染个体中,N 的 IgG 阳性率 (80.9%) 高于 S (42.8%),与大流行前对照相比,N 特异性 IgG 水平显着升高(p 值 <0.05)。接种疫苗的 队列研究 对两种低 IgM 水平的抗原表现出高 IgG 阳性率 (83-100%),并且总体 IgG 和亚类反应相对于大流行前对照显着升高(p 值 <0.05)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,自然感染会诱导偏向核衣壳抗原的协调体液反应,而 疫苗接种 则会引发强大的多亚类抗体反应,在抗原识别和亚类分布方面具有平台依赖性差异。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果支持使用核衣壳特异性抗体作为最近 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染的标记,并强调了解 疫苗 诱导的 免疫应答 中平台依赖性差异对于改进 监测 和 疫苗 发育的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于第一波大流行的血清,并未考虑长期免疫或变异特异性反应,但由于使用经过验证的 ELISA 方法直接比较抗体反应,因此证据充足。

papers.title_zh: 自然 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染后的核衣壳和刺突特异性同种型体液 免疫应答 与国药集团、科兴和阿斯利康的 疫苗接种 的比较分析。
papers.source_body_en: The diversity of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) vaccine platforms and widespread natural exposure have created a complex landscape of humoral immunity requiring detailed characterization. Here, we compare nucleocapsid (N)- and spike (S)-specific antibody responses in sera from infected humans (IH) during the first pandemic wave (April–August 2020) and in vaccine recipients (Sinopharm, Sinovac, or AstraZeneca) using commercial ELISA kits. Strong positive correlations were observed between S- and N-specific antibody responses, particularly for IgG and its subclasses. Vaccinated cohorts exhibited high IgG positivity rate (83–100%) against both antigens with low IgM levels, and overall IgG and subclass responses were significantly elevated relative to pre-pandemic controls ( p -value <0.05), with consistently strong inter-antigen correlations across groups. Overall, natural infection induces a coordinated humoral response biased toward the nucleocapsid antigen, supporting its utility as a marker of recent infection, whereas vaccination elicits a robust multi-subclass antibody response with platform-dependent differences in antigen recognition and subclass distribution.

papers.title: A single Omicron mutation reshapes ORF3a-driven host-cell remodelling
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT SARS-CoV-2 ORF3a remodels host membranes, but the structural basis and metabolic consequences of this process remain unclear. Here, we combine complementary imaging approaches to define ORF3a function at nanometric scale, identifying underlying mechanisms, and determining how Omicron variant rewire this activity. ORF3a from the ancestral Wuhan strain disrupts Golgi cisternae, drives the formation of ORF3a dense vesicles, remodels mitochondrial architecture, and promotes lipid droplet expansion. Multi-omics analyses further reveal selective triacylglycerol accumulation linked to DGAT1 upregulation, which we validate pharmacologically through DGAT1 inhibition. In contrast, Omicron ORF3a variant, despite carrying only the Thr223Ile substitution within the β7-β8 loop at the bottom of the ‘cytosolic domain’, induced a dramatic phenotypic shift: ORF3a localizes to multivesicular bodies, preserves Golgi architecture, and fails to induce lipid accumulation. All together, these results identify ORF3a as a regulator of membrane organization and lipid homeostasis, showing how minimal sequence variation rewires host-cell remodelling.

papers.title: Supplementation of αKG along with TGFβ/HIF1α antagonist rescues lung fibrosis in mice with severe SARS-CoV-2 infection
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary fibrosis and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) are the clinical challenges among patients with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), affecting ~ 10% of the survivors worldwide. PASC manifestations include pulmonary fibrosis, impaired respiratory function, and long-term morbidity. Recent WHO reports from 83 countries also describe severe morbidity among COVID-19 survivors associated with PASC, indicating an unmet need to address the issue. We developed a mouse model showing the above disease pathophysiology, and investigated the related signalling molecules, with a focus on developing targeted treatment strategies against it. METHODS: We developed the mild and severe SARS-CoV-2 infection mice models. We took the opportunity to transiently express high/low levels of hACE2 in the airways and lungs of the mice, to manipulate infection severity and longer survivability. The severe infection model developed ARDS pathogenesis and pulmonary fibrosis, limiting respiratory functions (assessed by dual-chamber plethysmography), and survived beyond 30 DPI. The signalling molecules of these pathogenic pathways were identified from related tissue/blood samples of the mice using mass spectrometry-based proteome analysis, histopathology, immunoblotting and flow cytometry. RESULTS: The proteomic analysis revealed key pathways driving epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and pulmonary fibrosis in mice lungs. Elevated expression of P-AKT, TGFβ and HIF1α supported the severity of ARDS and fibrosis in lungs at 15 as well as 30 DPI. We developed a treatment strategy by targeting the above signalling molecules. Treatment with dietary alpha-ketoglutarate (1% αKG daily), known suppressor of P-AKT, along with inhibitor to TGFβ (SB431542,10 mg/kg BW) or HIF1α (CAY10585, 10 mg/kg BW/daily, delivered intraperitoneally) till 7 DPI, significantly reduced EMT and fibrosis by suppressing the PAKT: TGFβ:HIF1α signalling, and finally improved mice survivability (50%) beyond 50 DPI with a restored pulmonary function. CONCLUSION: The study thus demonstrated the upregulation signalling molecules like P-AKT, TGFβ and HIF1α and their association with pulmonary fibrosis in mice after severe SARS-CoV-2 infection. Further, the inhibition of the above pathophysiology by the co-administration of αKG along with HIF1α/TGFβ antagonist highlighted a targeted therapeutic strategy against it. Importantly, for the first time, our study described the HIF1α axis as the therapeutic target in rescuing post-acute sequelae such as ARDS and fibrosis in mice with severe SARS-CoV-2 infection.

Further, the inhibition of the above pathophysiology by the co-administration of αKG along with HIF1α/TGFβ antagonist highlighted a targeted therapeutic strategy against it. Importantly, for the first time, our study described the HIF1α axis as the therapeutic target in rescuing post-acute sequelae such as ARDS and fibrosis in mice with severe SARS-CoV-2 infection.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们开发了轻度和重度 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染小鼠模型。我们开发了显示上述疾病病理生理学的小鼠模型,并研究了相关的信号分子,重点是开发针对它的靶向 治疗 策略。

elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告局限性或证据强度。

papers.title: The SARS-CoV-2 S2′-helix compared to stem-helix confers higher genetic barrier to antibody resistance
papers.abstract: Understanding the potential for resistance to antibodies targeting conserved epitopes on the coronavirus spike protein is essential for developing broad-spectrum antivirals. The S2′-helix and stem helix represent two key conserved epitopes across multiple coronaviruses, with the S2′-helix being broadly conserved throughout the coronavirus subfamily and the stem helix primarily conserved among betacoronaviruses. Here, we demonstrate that the S2′-helix in SARS-CoV-2 possesses a higher genetic barrier to antibody resistance than the stem helix. Potent escape mutations in the stem helix, including D1153G, Y1155S, F1156L and F1156V, were selected under antibody pressure, and variants such as S1147L, E1151D, D1153G, D1153H, D1153Y and Y1155H were frequently identified in naturally circulating strains. These mutations completely abolished neutralization by some stem helix-targeting antibodies. In contrast, under pressure from S2′-helix-targeting antibodies, we did not detect clear viral escape. Only one naturally occurring mutation in the S2′-helix, L822F, was observed at considerable frequency, it weakly or mildly reduced but did not abolish neutralizing activity. Furthermore, combination therapy with S2′-helix-targeting antibodies synergistically suppressed the emergence of escape mutants selected by stem helix-directed antibodies. Our findings underscore the S2′-helix as a promising target for the design of broadly protective coronavirus therapeutics with a reduced risk of viral escape.

papers.title: Directed evolution of a stem-helix-targeting antibody enables MERS-CoV cross-neutralization through enhanced binding affinity.
papers.abstract: Abstract Broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) targeting conserved regions of the betacoronavirus spike are important for pan-betacoronavirus protection and pandemic preparedness. Here, we report on the isolation of a human monoclonal antibody, CC65.1, from a SARS-CoV-2 convalescent donor that targets the conserved S2 stem helix region. CC65.1 neutralizes various sarbecoviruses, including SARS-CoV-2, and binds the MERS-CoV spike but lacks MERS-CoV-neutralizing activity due to insufficient binding affinity. We utilized directed evolution to enhance the binding affinity of CC65.1 for the MERS-CoV S2 stem helix, yielding engineered antibody variants with newly acquired MERS-CoV-neutralizing activity. High-resolution structural analysis reveals key paratope mutations that optimize binding and stabilize epitope engagement. Our findings demonstrate the potential of rational antibody engineering to expand bnAb breadth across divergent betacoronaviruses. This work supports the development of engineered bnAbs and S2-targeted vaccines for broad betacoronavirus countermeasures and highlights strategies to achieve cross-lineage immunity for future pandemic threats. Author Summary The persistent emergence of new SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern that evade neutralizing antibody responses and other zoonotic betacoronaviruses with pandemic potential have provided strong motivation to develop broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) that target more conserved regions of the spike protein in sarbecoviruses and other betacoronaviruses. Here, we employed a directed evolution strategy to engineer the sarbecovirus-neutralizing antibody CC65.1, which targets the conserved S2 stem helix, to enhance its binding affinity with the MERS-CoV stem helix region, thereby conferring MERS-CoV neutralization. High-resolution structural studies of engineered CC65.1 revealed that key mutations reshape the paratope to better accommodate and stabilize the MERS-CoV S2 stem helix, resulting in increased binding affinity and neutralization potency. This study emphasizes the critical role of affinity maturation in expanding neutralization breadth and provides valuable insights for design of bnAbs to prevent and treat pandemic threats by betacoronaviruses.

papers.title: Clinical outcomes in patients hospitalized for COVID-19 in the periods of non-Omicron and Omicron variant dominance.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Omicron is known for its higher transmissibility and milder respiratory symptoms than those of other SARS-CoV-2 variants. How comorbidities contribute to mortality outcomes in Omicron-related COVID-19 remains unclear. This study compared clinical features and outcomes between Omicron and non-Omicron variants and identified risk factors for in-hospital mortality. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted from April 2020 to September 2022. Patients with COVID-19 infection were divided into Omicron and non-Omicron groups. Demographic data, laboratory results, and treatment information were collected and analyzed. Clinical outcomes for different variants were analyzed. RESULTS: The Omicron group had a greater burden of comorbidities but exhibited lower COVID-19 disease severity and fewer complications than did the non-Omicron group. Overall mortality was relatively high in the Omicron group, primarily due to non-COVID-related causes. In multivariate analysis, a Charlson comorbidity index score of ≥3 (odds ratio [OR] = 4.60, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.94-10.91, p < 0.001), severe or critical COVID-19 (OR = 1.60, 95% CI = 1.24-2.07, p < 0.001), a high white blood cell count (OR = 1.00, 95% CI = 1.00-1.00, p = 0.021), and a high C-reactive protein level (OR = 1.01, 95% CI = 1.00-1.01, p = 0.003) emerged as positive predictors of COVID-19-related mortality. CONCLUSION: Severe or critical COVID-19 and a Charlson comorbidity index score of ≥3 were independently associated with high in-hospital mortality. Intensive monitoring and early intervention should be prioritized for high-risk groups to improve clinical outcomes.

papers.title_zh: Clinical outcomes in patients hospitalized for COVID-19 in the periods of non-Omicron and Omicron variant dominance.
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Omicron is known for its higher transmissibility and milder respiratory symptoms than those of other SARS-CoV-2 variants. How comorbidities contribute to mortality outcomes in Omicron-related COVID-19 remains unclear. This study compared clinical features and outcomes between Omicron and non-Omicron variants and identified risk factors for in-hospital mortality. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted from April 2020 to September 2022. Patients with COVID-19 infection were divided into Omicron and non-Omicron groups. Demographic data, laboratory results, and treatment information were collected and analyzed. Clinical outcomes for different variants were analyzed. RESULTS: The Omicron group had a greater burden of comorbidities but exhibited lower COVID-19 disease severity and fewer complications than did the non-Omicron group. Overall mortality was relatively high in the Omicron group, primarily due to non-COVID-related causes. In multivariate analysis, a Charlson comorbidity index score of ≥3 (odds ratio [OR] = 4.60, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.94-10.91, p < 0.001), severe or critical COVID-19 (OR = 1.60, 95% CI = 1.24-2.07, p < 0.001), a high white blood cell count (OR = 1.00, 95% CI = 1.00-1.00, p = 0.021), and a high C-reactive protein level (OR = 1.01, 95% CI = 1.00-1.01, p = 0.003) emerged as positive predictors of COVID-19-related mortality. CONCLUSION: Severe or critical COVID-19 and a Charlson comorbidity index score of ≥3 were independently associated with high in-hospital mortality. Intensive monitoring and early intervention should be prioritized for high-risk groups to improve clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Secondary Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis Triggered by Mixed Plasmodium spp. and SARS-CoV-2 Coinfection
papers.abstract: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome that may be triggered by infectious diseases, including malaria and viral infections. A case of mixed Plasmodium vivax and Plasmodium falciparum infection concomitant with severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 in a patient who developed secondary HLH is described in the present study. Malaria was acquired in the endemic state of Mato Grosso, Brazil, but diagnosed in Macaé, Rio de Janeiro, a nonendemic region. The patient presented with high fever, pancytopenia, hypertriglyceridemia, and hyperferritinemia. Bone marrow aspirate revealed hemophagocytosis. The patient met six of the eight HLH-2004 criteria and had an HScore indicating a high probability of secondary HLH. Recovery was achieved after the initiation of antimalarial and corticosteroid therapies. This case suggests that parasitic and viral infections may synergistically trigger immunologic “second hits,” promoting macrophage hyperactivation. Recognition of overlapping infections, particularly outside endemic areas, may facilitate earlier diagnosis and timely management of secondary HLH.
papers.journal: The American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究探讨了为什么继发性噬血细胞性淋巴组织细胞增多症 (HLH) 在疟疾和 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(一种由传染病引发的危及生命的高炎症综合征)混合感染期间可能出现。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一篇 病例报告 文章,描述了一名患有间日疟原虫和恶性疟原虫混合疟疾以及 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 合并感染并出现继发性 HLH 的患者。
elements_zh.methods: 患者在流行地区感染后在非流行地区被诊断为疟疾,并评估临床和实验室特征以满足 HLH-2004 标准并计算 HScore。
elements_zh.main_results: 该患者出现高热、全血细胞减少、高甘油三酯血症、高铁蛋白血症,骨髓穿刺显示有噬血细胞,符合 HLH-2004 八项标准中的六项,HScore 表明继发性 HLH 的可能性很高。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将此病例解释为表明寄生虫和病毒感染可能协同触发免疫第二次打击,促进巨噬细胞过度激活,并强调了识别流行区外重叠感染以促进早期 诊断 的新颖性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,临床医生应考虑重叠感染,特别是在非流行地区,以便及时进行 诊断 和继发性 HLH 的管理。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于单个 病例报告,这限制了普遍性并排除了因果推断,导致对更广泛结论的信心较低。

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一篇 病例报告 文章,描述了一名患有间日疟原虫和恶性疟原虫混合疟疾以及 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 合并感染并出现继发性 HLH 的患者。

papers.title: Long-term angiogenic and thromboinflammatory signatures in post-COVID-19 syndrome.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Post-COVID-19 syndrome is a major long-term sequela of severe SARS-CoV-2 infection, potentially involving persistent angiogenic and thromboinflammatory dysfunction, though long-term biomarker behavior remains unclear. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the evolution of angiogenic and thromboinflammatory biomarkers in post-COVID-19 syndrome patients. METHODS: This ambispective cohort study was conducted at the National Institute of Respiratory Diseases in Mexico City. Thirty-two adults hospitalized for severe or critical COVID-19 in 2020 were followed for three and a half years. Paired plasma samples were collected during hospitalization and at long-term follow-up. Endothelial dysfunction markers included soluble P-selectin, vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 2, vascular endothelial growth factor D, and angiopoietin-1. Hemostasis was assessed by prothrombin time. Acute-phase proteins alpha-2-macroglobulin and haptoglobin were measured via immunoassay. Persistent symptoms were documented at follow-up. RESULTS: At three and a half years, persistent symptoms were common: fatigue in sixty-five point 6%, dyspnea in sixty-two point 5%, and concentration difficulties in sixty-five point 6%. Vascular endothelial growth factor D and angiopoietin-1 remained elevated. Alpha-2-macroglobulin stayed high, and prothrombin time was prolonged in a subset of patients. CONCLUSIONS: Severe COVID-19 survivors show sustained angiogenic dysregulation and thromboinflammatory imbalance. Elevated vascular endothelial growth factor D and angiopoietin-1 indicate ongoing angiogenic perturbations, while increased alpha-2-macroglobulin and prolonged prothrombin time reflect persistent coagulation disturbances. These biomarkers may help identify long-term vascular alterations in post-COVID-19 syndrome.

Hemostasis was assessed by prothrombin time. Acute-phase proteins alpha-2-macroglobulin and haptoglobin were measured via immunoassay. Persistent symptoms were documented at follow-up. RESULTS: At three and a half years, persistent symptoms were common: fatigue in sixty-five point 6%, dyspnea in sixty-two point 5%, and concentration difficulties in sixty-five point 6%. Vascular endothelial growth factor D and angiopoietin-1 remained elevated. Alpha-2-macroglobulin stayed high, and prothrombin time was prolonged in a subset of patients. Elevated vascular endothelial growth factor D and angiopoietin-1 indicate ongoing angiogenic perturbations, while increased alpha-2-macroglobulin and prolonged prothrombin time reflect persistent coagulation disturbances. These biomarkers may help identify long-term vascular alterations in post-COVID-19 syndrome.

papers.title: Workplace Violence Before and During the COVID-19 Pandemic: Occupational Disparities in Nonfatal Violent Victimization.
papers.abstract: This study sought to understand the COVID-19 pandemic's impact on nonfatal workplace violence (WPV) experiences of workers in different occupational groups in the United States. The 2017 to 2022 National Crime Victimization Survey data were used to generate national nonfatal WPV rates in the United States for seven occupational groups. We used a quantitative approach to compare the WPV rates across occupational groups before and during the pandemic in light of changes in the routine activities of the U.S. First, average annual WPV rates by occupational group were compared across study years to identify temporal patterns. Second, average WPV rates for the three pre-pandemic years (2017-2019) and the three pandemic years (2020-2022) were compared to assess changes associated with the pandemic. Third, paired samples t -tests were conducted to determine whether differences in WPV rates between the pre-pandemic and pandemic periods were statistically significant for each occupational group. Our analysis of overall patterns revealed several temporal shifts: WPV rates sharply declined in the first pandemic year, surged in the second year, and shifted downward again in the third year. We also found that WPV rates varied across occupational groups and pandemic years, suggesting that these trends reflect differential changes in working environments across occupational groups during distinct phases of the pandemic. These findings highlight the complex and heterogenous impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on WPV and underscore the importance of considering occupational and contextual differences when developing policies and interventions to mitigate WPV during public health emergencies.

analysis.scope_and_question: Workplace violence (WPV) experiences among U.S. workers across seven occupational groups during the COVID-19 pandemic, focusing on temporal changes in nonfatal victimization rates and occupational disparities.

papers.title: Machine learning-based prediction of SARS-CoV-2 bioactivity: integrating IC50 regression and activity classification using multi-task neural networks
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of compound bioactivity is essential for accelerating antiviral drug discovery and reducing experimental costs. Machine learning (ML) methods have shown considerable promise in modeling structure–activity relationships and compound potency. In this study, we present an integrated ML framework for predicting IC50 and pIC50 values of compounds active against SARS-CoV-2, key indicators of antiviral potency. The proposed framework comprises three complementary approaches: (i) a regression model for quantitative IC50 prediction validated against experimental data; (ii) a classification model that categorizes compounds into active and inactive classes to support compound prioritization; and (iii) a multi-task neural network that jointly performs IC50 regression and activity classification, enhancing predictive performance and interpretability. A distinctive feature of this work is the incorporation of ligand efficiency (LE) as a criterion for activity classification, offering an alternative perspective on compound prioritization that has not been previously explored in SARS-CoV-2 bioactivity modeling. The proposed models demonstrate strong predictive capability, achieving a coefficient of determination (\documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$R^2$$\end{document}) of 0.77 using a neural network with feature selection, while the Random Forest classifier attains an accuracy, precision, and recall of approximately 0.92. These results highlight the potential of integrated regression, classification, and multi-task learning approaches as scalable and cost-effective tools for SARS-CoV-2 bioactivity prediction and antiviral drug discovery.

papers.title: COVID-19 Vaccination Refusal Among Cancer Survivors in the United States: A Scoping Review
papers.abstract: Cancer survivors face an elevated risk of severe COVID-19 outcomes and were prioritized for vaccination, yet reported rates of vaccination refusal in this population vary widely. The objective of this scoping review was to map the available evidence on COVID-19 vaccination refusal among adult cancer survivors in the United States, to characterize the reported barriers and enablers, and to examine how differences in measurement account for variation in the reported estimates. PubMed, EBSCOhost, CINAHL, medRxiv, and Google Scholar were searched for studies published between 1 December 2020 and 30 April 2026 reporting primary data on COVID-19 vaccination refusal among U.S. adults with a current or previous cancer diagnosis. Findings were charted and summarized descriptively. Six sources comprising 3344 participants met the eligibility criteria. Reported refusal ranged from 7.3% to 39.0%, a more than fivefold difference, with a median of 14.7%. This variation corresponded closely to what each source measured: declination of an offered vaccine, likelihood of acceptance on a Likert scale, hesitancy assessed before vaccines were widely available, or observed non-receipt of any dose. Barriers included concerns about vaccine safety, efficacy, and interaction with cancer treatment, mistrust of science and government, and low perceived need; clinician recommendation was the most consistent enabler. Estimates of vaccination refusal in this population are not directly comparable and should be interpreted alongside the construct measured.

elements_en.scope_and_question: The review examines COVID-19 vaccination refusal among adult cancer survivors in the United States, focusing on the variability in reported refusal rates and the factors influencing vaccine hesitancy in this high-risk population.
elements_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: This scoping review searched PubMed, EBSCOhost, CINAHL, medRxiv, and Google Scholar for studies published between 1 December 2020 and 30 April 2026 that reported primary data on COVID-19 vaccination refusal among U.S. adults with a current or previous cancer diagnosis. Six sources comprising 3344 participants were included, and findings were charted and summarized descriptively.
elements_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Reported COVID-19 vaccination refusal among adult cancer survivors in the U.S. ranged from 7.3% to 39.0%, with a median of 14.7%, reflecting a more than fivefold difference. This variation was closely tied to the construct measured, such as declination of an offered vaccine, likelihood of acceptance on a Likert scale, hesitancy assessed before vaccine availability, or observed non-receipt of any dose.
elements_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights that estimates of vaccination refusal in this population are not directly comparable due to differences in measurement constructs, which complicates the interpretation of refusal rates and their implications for public health strategies.
elements_en.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should standardize measurement constructs for vaccination refusal to enable accurate comparisons and inform targeted interventions. Clinician recommendations emerged as a consistent enabler of vaccination, suggesting that healthcare provider engagement could reduce refusal rates in this vulnerable population.

papers.title_zh: COVID-19 Vaccination Refusal Among Cancer Survivors in the United States: A Scoping Review
papers.source_body_en: Cancer survivors face an elevated risk of severe COVID-19 outcomes and were prioritized for vaccination, yet reported rates of vaccination refusal in this population vary widely. The objective of this scoping review was to map the available evidence on COVID-19 vaccination refusal among adult cancer survivors in the United States, to characterize the reported barriers and enablers, and to examine how differences in measurement account for variation in the reported estimates. PubMed, EBSCOhost, CINAHL, medRxiv, and Google Scholar were searched for studies published between 1 December 2020 and 30 April 2026 reporting primary data on COVID-19 vaccination refusal among U.S. adults with a current or previous cancer diagnosis. Findings were charted and summarized descriptively. Six sources comprising 3344 participants met the eligibility criteria. Reported refusal ranged from 7.3% to 39.0%, a more than fivefold difference, with a median of 14.7%. This variation corresponded closely to what each source measured: declination of an offered vaccine, likelihood of acceptance on a Likert scale, hesitancy assessed before vaccines were widely available, or observed non-receipt of any dose. Barriers included concerns about vaccine safety, efficacy, and interaction with cancer treatment, mistrust of science and government, and low perceived need; clinician recommendation was the most consistent enabler. Estimates of vaccination refusal in this population are not directly comparable and should be interpreted alongside the construct measured.

papers.title: Proteomic and Phosphoproteomic Characteristics of Multiple Brain Regions in Rhesus Macaques After SARS-CoV-2 Infection.
papers.abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant is more contagious than the original Alpha variant and can still cause neurological symptoms, including cognitive impairment. To gain a deeper understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying these neurological effects, this study was conducted. Proteomic and phosphoproteomic analyses were carried out utilizing LC-MS/MS. Samples included brainstem, cerebellum, frontal lobe, occipital lobe, parietal lobe, and temporal lobe from SARS-CoV-2 Omicron-infected and noninfected control rhesus macaques. Infection with Omicron resulted in inflammatory responses across all six brain regions, and significant regional-specific molecular alterations were observed. Proteomic and phosphoproteomic analyses revealed extensive abnormalities in immune activation, synaptic function, DNA repair, and signaling pathways across different brain regions. We further predicted key kinases and identified candidate proteins with significantly altered expression. This study reveals region-specific inflammatory and signaling signatures in the brain following Omicron infection. The recognized kinases and proteins with abnormal regulation serve as potential candidates for drug discovery. This can aid in formulating new therapeutic approaches for neurological issues related to COVID-19.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the proteomic and phosphoproteomic changes in multiple brain regions of rhesus macaques infected with the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant. The research was motivated by the variant's increased contagiousness and its potential to cause neurological symptoms such as cognitive impairment. Using LC-MS/MS, the study identified inflammatory responses and region-specific molecular alterations across six brain regions. These findings reveal distinct inflammatory and signaling patterns in the brain following Omicron infection, which could guide future therapeutic approaches for neurological issues related to COVID-19. However, the study is based on abstract-level data and lacks detailed statistical or mechanistic analyses, limiting the confidence in its conclusions to a moderate level.

papers.title: SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid induces hyperinflammation and vascular leakage through the Toll-like receptor signaling axis in macrophages.
papers.abstract: A substantial proportion of hospitalized COVID-19 patients require ICU admission, often associated with an imbalance between antiviral responses and inflammatory signaling leading to uncontrolled cytokine secretion. The SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid (N) protein is a known immune antagonist, but its role in macrophage-driven cytokine storms is unclear. We demonstrate that N functions in a stimulus-specific manner, specifically amplifying extracellular and dampening intracellular RNA sensing. Moreover, we show that this is a conserved feature of pathogenic betacoronaviruses through distinct mechanisms. Our interaction networks with SARS-CoV-2 variant N proteins suggest that the Delta variant N drives inflammation through interactions with several proteins, most notably, cGAS. Profiling of secreted cytokines revealed that N disrupts the secretome in a variant-specific manner. Most notably, we found that supernatants from the Delta variant N-expressing macrophages dramatically disrupt heart endothelial barriers, implicating N in COVID-19-associated cardiac complications. Our findings highlight N-mediated immune imbalance as a driver of severe COVID-19 and identify N as a promising therapeutic target to mitigate hyperinflammation.

The SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid (N) protein is a known immune antagonist, but its role in macrophage-driven cytokine storms is unclear. We demonstrate that N functions in a stimulus-specific manner, specifically amplifying extracellular and dampening intracellular RNA sensing. Moreover, we show that this is a conserved feature of pathogenic betacoronaviruses through distinct mechanisms. Our interaction networks with SARS-CoV-2 variant N proteins suggest that the Delta variant N drives inflammation through interactions with several proteins, most notably, cGAS. Profiling of secreted cytokines revealed that N disrupts the secretome in a variant-specific manner. Most notably, we found that supernatants from the Delta variant N-expressing macrophages dramatically disrupt heart endothelial barriers, implicating N in COVID-19-associated cardiac complications. Our findings highlight N-mediated immune imbalance as a driver of severe COVID-19 and identify N as a promising therapeutic target to mitigate hyperinflammation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses why some SARS-CoV-2 infections progress to severe COVID-19 with hyperinflammation and vascular complications, noting that hospitalized patients often require ICU care due to an imbalance between antiviral responses and inflammatory signaling leading to uncontrolled cytokine secretion.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research investigates the role of the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid (N) protein in macrophage-driven cytokine storms, focusing on its immune-modulatory functions and variant-specific effects.
analysis.methods: The authors examined how the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein modulates extracellular and intracellular RNA sensing in macrophages, including its interactions with cGAS and effects on cytokine secretion profiles across SARS-CoV-2 variants.
analysis.main_results: Profiling of secreted cytokines revealed variant-specific disruption of the secretome by the nucleocapsid protein, with supernatants from macrophages expressing the Delta variant N protein causing dramatic disruption of heart endothelial barriers.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings identify the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein as a driver of severe COVID-19 through immune imbalance, highlighting its conserved role across pathogenic betacoronaviruses and variant-specific mechanisms, including interactions with cGAS.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study suggests that targeting the nucleocapsid protein could mitigate hyperinflammation in severe COVID-19 and potentially address cardiac complications associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to abstract-level data and lacks detailed experimental context, sample sizes, or statistical analyses, which constrains the strength of the conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid (N) protein as a driver of macrophage-mediated hyperinflammation and vascular leakage, a hallmark of severe COVID-19. The authors demonstrate that N amplifies extracellular RNA sensing while dampening intracellular responses, a conserved feature among pathogenic betacoronaviruses. Variant-specific analyses reveal that the Delta variant N protein disrupts cytokine secretion and disrupts heart endothelial barriers, implicating N in COVID-19-associated cardiac complications. The findings suggest N as a therapeutic target to mitigate hyperinflammation, though the evidence is confined to abstract-level data and lacks detailed experimental validation.

papers.title: When reoxygenation fails: a dynamical model of HIF-1$$\alpha $$-mediated metabolic breakdown under hypoxia and SARS-CoV-2 infection
papers.abstract: Cells normally combine glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) to meet energy demands, but this balance shifts under pathological conditions. During SARS-CoV-2 infection, hypoxia, viral entry, and elevated tissue lactate alter cellular metabolism. To explore these effects, we propose a parsimonious mathematical model describing how oxygen levels, viral infiltration, and extracellular lactate jointly regulate metabolic balance through HIF-1 α protein, inside the cell, accounting for lactate's biphasic, non-monotonic influence on glycolysis. Model simulations reveal a single steady state whose position on the glycolysis-OXPHOS phase plane depends on environmental conditions, namely, oxygen concentration, infection, and extracellular lactate. We identify four metabolic regimes, determined by sufficiency of energy production and the driving process (OXPHOS or glycolysis). Decreasing the oxygen shifts cells from OXPHOS to glycolysis dominance in both infected and non-infected states, but infected cells may become energy-deficient even with sufficient oxygen due to virus-induced mitochondrial damage. Rising extracellular lactate initially promotes glycolysis but ultimately suppresses it at high levels, pushing cells into severe energy deficit with inhibited glycolysis. Simulations of reoxygenation exhibit hysteresis: cells pass through an energy-deficient zone during hypoxia onset but return through a safer trajectory when oxygen is restored; a vulnerability is higher in infected cells. Overall, the model clarifies metabolic trajectories during viral infection, suggesting that early hypoxia is particularly dangerous and that severe acidosis can further collapse energy production. Preventing or rapidly reversing hypoxia in respiratory infection may protect cells from energy failure and limit harmful lactate accumulation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand how SARS-CoV-2 infection alters cellular metabolism under hypoxia, particularly the interplay between oxygen levels, viral infiltration, and extracellular lactate in regulating metabolic balance through HIF-1α protein.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed a mathematical model to simulate metabolic dynamics in cells under hypoxia and SARS-CoV-2 infection, focusing on the regulation of glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) by HIF-1α protein.
analysis.methods: The model incorporated oxygen concentration, viral infiltration, and extracellular lactate as variables to describe their joint regulation of metabolic balance, with particular attention to lactate's biphasic influence on glycolysis.
analysis.main_results: Model simulations revealed a single steady state on the glycolysis-OXPHOS phase plane, influenced by oxygen concentration, infection, and extracellular lactate. Four metabolic regimes were identified based on energy production sufficiency and the dominant process (OXPHOS or glycolysis).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that decreasing oxygen shifts cells toward glycolysis dominance, but infected cells may still face energy deficiency due to mitochondrial damage. The model highlights the dangers of early hypoxia and the potential for severe acidosis to collapse energy production.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that preventing or reversing hypoxia in respiratory infections could protect cells from energy failure and reduce harmful lactate accumulation, offering insights for therapeutic strategies in managing SARS-CoV-2-related metabolic disturbances.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a mathematical model, which may not fully capture in vivo complexities. However, the model provides a clear framework for understanding metabolic shifts during SARS-CoV-2 infection, with a moderate level of confidence based on the abstract-only evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a mathematical model to explore how SARS-CoV-2 infection affects cellular metabolism under hypoxia, focusing on the role of HIF-1α protein in regulating glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS). The model identifies four metabolic regimes and demonstrates that infected cells are more vulnerable to energy deficiency even with sufficient oxygen. It also highlights the biphasic effect of extracellular lactate on glycolysis and the hysteresis observed during reoxygenation. The results suggest that early hypoxia is particularly dangerous and that severe acidosis can further impair energy production. These findings have implications for understanding metabolic changes in SARS-CoV-2 infection and could inform strategies to prevent energy failure and lactate accumulation. The study's reliance on a mathematical model limits its direct applicability to real-world scenarios, but it provides a valuable framework for further research.

papers.title_zh: 当复氧失败时:缺氧和 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染下 HIF-1$$\alpha $$ 介导的代谢分解的动力学模型
papers.source_body_en: Cells normally combine glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) to meet energy demands, but this balance shifts under pathological conditions. During SARS-CoV-2 infection, hypoxia, viral entry, and elevated tissue lactate alter cellular metabolism. To explore these effects, we propose a parsimonious mathematical model describing how oxygen levels, viral infiltration, and extracellular lactate jointly regulate metabolic balance through HIF-1 α protein, inside the cell, accounting for lactate's biphasic, non-monotonic influence on glycolysis. Model simulations reveal a single steady state whose position on the glycolysis-OXPHOS phase plane depends on environmental conditions, namely, oxygen concentration, infection, and extracellular lactate. We identify four metabolic regimes, determined by sufficiency of energy production and the driving process (OXPHOS or glycolysis). Decreasing the oxygen shifts cells from OXPHOS to glycolysis dominance in both infected and non-infected states, but infected cells may become energy-deficient even with sufficient oxygen due to virus-induced mitochondrial damage. Rising extracellular lactate initially promotes glycolysis but ultimately suppresses it at high levels, pushing cells into severe energy deficit with inhibited glycolysis. Simulations of reoxygenation exhibit hysteresis: cells pass through an energy-deficient zone during hypoxia onset but return through a safer trajectory when oxygen is restored; a vulnerability is higher in infected cells. Overall, the model clarifies metabolic trajectories during viral infection, suggesting that early hypoxia is particularly dangerous and that severe acidosis can further collapse energy production. Preventing or rapidly reversing hypoxia in respiratory infection may protect cells from energy failure and limit harmful lactate accumulation.
papers.abstract_zh: 细胞通常结合糖酵解和氧化磷酸化(OXPHOS)来满足能量需求,但这种平衡在病理条件下会发生变化。在 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染期间,缺氧、病毒进入和组织乳酸升高会改变细胞代谢。为了探索这些影响,我们提出了一个简洁的数学模型,描述氧水平、病毒浸润和细胞外乳酸如何通过细胞内的 HIF-1 α 蛋白共同调节代谢平衡,解释乳酸对糖酵解的双相、非单调影响。模型模拟揭示了单一稳态,其在糖酵解-OXPHOS 相平面上的位置取决于环境条件,即氧浓度、感染和细胞外乳酸。我们确定了四种代谢模式,由能量产生的充足性和驱动过程(OXPHOS 或糖酵解)决定。在感染和未感染状态下,氧气的减少会使细胞从 OXPHOS 转变为糖酵解主导,但由于病毒诱导的线粒体损伤,即使氧气充足,受感染的细胞也可能会变得能量不足。细胞外乳酸的增加最初会促进糖酵解,但最终会在高水平上抑制糖酵解,从而使细胞陷入严重的能量不足,糖酵解受到抑制。再氧合的模拟表现出滞后现象:细胞在缺氧开始时穿过能量缺乏区域,但在氧气恢复时通过更安全的轨迹返回;受感染细胞的脆弱性更高。总体而言,该模型阐明了病毒感染期间的代谢轨迹,表明早期缺氧特别危险,严重的酸中毒会进一步破坏能量产生。预防或快速逆转呼吸道感染中的缺氧可以保护细胞免受能量衰竭并限制有害的乳酸积累。

papers.title: Impact of SARS-CoV-2 infection on the progression of Alzheimer's disease: A prospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: Background SARS-CoV-2 infection is associated with neurological sequelae and may accelerate Alzheimer's disease (AD) progression through neuroinflammation and protein aggregation. However, longitudinal evidence regarding the cognitive impact of COVID-19 in patients with AD remains scarce, and this interaction requires further clarification. Objective To explore whether COVID-19 accelerates cognitive decline in patients with AD. Methods A total of 120 participants were enrolled, including 63 in the COVID-19 group and 57 in the non-COVID-19 group. The primary outcomes were disease decline and disease deterioration over three months, assessed using CDR-SB. Disease deterioration indicated clinically meaningful worsening, whereas disease decline captured subtler progression. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for demographic, clinical, lifestyle, genetic, and disease severity factors. Overlap-Weighted Propensity Score Matching was additionally performed to reduce confounding during the 3-month follow-up. Results COVID-19 significantly increased the risk of disease decline (OR = 10.39, 95% CI:3.87 to 27.87, p < 0.001) and disease deterioration (OR = 10.37, 95% CI: 2.71 to 39.65, p = 0.001). APOE ε4 carrier status was associated with a higher risk of deterioration (OR = 1.72), while those with unknown APOE status exhibited an even greater risk (OR = 5.20, 95% CI:1.32 to 20.53, p = 0.019). Secondary analyses confirmed that COVID-19 patients experienced significantly greater increases in CDR-SB scores compared to non-COVID-19 patients. Conclusions SARS-CoV-2 infection was associated with greater short-term cognitive worsening over a three-month period in patients with AD, underscoring its potential public health relevance and the need for early surveillance to guide timely clinical management.

papers.title_zh: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染对阿尔茨海默病进展的影响:一项前瞻性 队列研究 研究。
papers.source_body_en: Background SARS-CoV-2 infection is associated with neurological sequelae and may accelerate Alzheimer's disease (AD) progression through neuroinflammation and protein aggregation. However, longitudinal evidence regarding the cognitive impact of COVID-19 in patients with AD remains scarce, and this interaction requires further clarification. Objective To explore whether COVID-19 accelerates cognitive decline in patients with AD. Methods A total of 120 participants were enrolled, including 63 in the COVID-19 group and 57 in the non-COVID-19 group. The primary outcomes were disease decline and disease deterioration over three months, assessed using CDR-SB. Disease deterioration indicated clinically meaningful worsening, whereas disease decline captured subtler progression. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for demographic, clinical, lifestyle, genetic, and disease severity factors. Overlap-Weighted Propensity Score Matching was additionally performed to reduce confounding during the 3-month follow-up. Results COVID-19 significantly increased the risk of disease decline (OR = 10.39, 95% CI:3.87 to 27.87, p < 0.001) and disease deterioration (OR = 10.37, 95% CI: 2.71 to 39.65, p = 0.001). APOE ε4 carrier status was associated with a higher risk of deterioration (OR = 1.72), while those with unknown APOE status exhibited an even greater risk (OR = 5.20, 95% CI:1.32 to 20.53, p = 0.019). Secondary analyses confirmed that COVID-19 patients experienced significantly greater increases in CDR-SB scores compared to non-COVID-19 patients. Conclusions SARS-CoV-2 infection was associated with greater short-term cognitive worsening over a three-month period in patients with AD, underscoring its potential public health relevance and the need for early surveillance to guide timely clinical management.

papers.title: Evaluation of One-Step amplicon-based targeted enrichment for SARS-CoV-2 whole-genome sequencing using the Midnight amplicon scheme.
papers.abstract: Genomic surveillance proved invaluable during the COVID-19 pandemic for tracking SARS-CoV-2 variants and guiding outbreak responses, underscoring the ongoing need to reduce whole-genome sequencing (WGS) costs and improve workflow efficiency to ensure accessibility in resource limited settings. Here, we evaluated a one-step reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) approach using the Midnight V2 primer scheme for targeted amplification of the SARS-CoV-2 genome, assessed its compatibility with Illumina sequencing, and compared its performance to a well-established two-step method. Initially, we determined optimal RT-PCR reaction conditions using the Midnight V2 primer panel for the one-step RT-PCR kit and scaled reaction volumes for both RT-PCR and library preparation. Clinical specimens (n=53) that had undergone routine WGS for surveillance purposes using the established two-step RT-PCR method were compared using the one-step RT-PCR assay. For samples with genome completeness greater than 70%, both methods gave comparable results with similar sequence coverage and 100% concordance for lineage assignment. Further investigation revealed a higher percentage of reads aligning to the SARS-CoV-2 genome with a greater depth of coverage using the one-step method compared to the two-step method. Finally, analysis of scaled one-step and library reaction volumes revealed significant cost savings for samples undergoing WGS. Overall, the results presented here verify the accuracy and reproducibility of one-step targeted amplification and offer an efficient and cost-effective workflow for routine SARS-CoV-2 genomic surveillance.

papers.title: Understanding the interactions and effect of environmental biofilms on SARS- CoV-2 viability on contact surfaces
papers.abstract: Abstract Aims To investigate the role of multispecies drain biofilms in SARS-CoV-2 infectivity and persistence on contact surfaces used in meat processing plants. Methods and Results Environmental drain biofilms from pork (n = 12) and beef (n = 22) processing plants were grown with and without SARS-CoV-2 on stainless steel (S.S.), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), tile, and galvanized steel (G.S.) at 7°C for 5 days. Biofilm biomass, viral RNA persistence, and viral infectivity were quantified and compared with controls. Surface type significantly influenced viral RNA persistence with PVC, tile, and particularly G.S. supporting increased SARS-CoV-2 RNA persistence relative to virus controls (p 2-fold; p < 0.01) while reducing growth of beef drain biofilms on S.S. (0.9–1.8 log reductions; p < 0.01). analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how multispecies drain biofilms affect SARS-CoV-2 infectivity and persistence on contact surfaces in meat processing plants. Biofilms from pork and beef processing facilities were grown on various materials at 7°C for 5 days with and without SARS-CoV-2. The results showed that surface type significantly influenced viral RNA persistence, with PVC, tile, and galvanized steel showing increased SARS-CoV-2 RNA persistence compared to virus controls (p < 0.01).
